source.title: Affine Grassmannians and the geometric Satake in mixed characteristic
source.version: Published90-page article; all pages read. Earlier arXiv passages collated only where specified.

summary: Zhu constructs the Witt vector affine Grassmannian as an ind-perfect algebraic space (Theorem 1.4), proves the geometric Satake equivalence in mixed characteristic (with a rational-coefficient Gelfand-trick proof of the commutativity constraint), identifies perfected Hodge-type Rapoport–Zink special fibres with affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties, and proves Rapoport's dimension formula (Theorem 3.1). Reviewed by REV-PAPER-ZHU-17 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 324 items (25 library, 45 planned, 254 missing). 75 mistakes are recorded (59 misprints, 7 gaps, 9 errors; 5 reach a stated result, 10 a proof). Theorem 3.10(3) needs b in G(W)σ(μ)(p)G(W) (E64), Theorems 0.5 and 3.1 need nonemptiness (E19), and the fundamental classes are canonical only up to powers of p (E27); the geometric Satake equivalence and the dimension formula stand. Not formalised.

declarations.statementRead:
/-- A truncated Witt vector over `R` is a vector of elements of `R`,
i.e., the first `n` coefficients of a Witt vector.
We will define operations on this type that are compatible with the (untruncated) Witt
vector operations.

`TruncatedWittVector p n R` takes a parameter `p : ℕ` that is not used in the definition.
In practice, this number `p` is assumed to be a prime number,
and under this assumption we construct a ring structure on `TruncatedWittVector p n R`.
(`TruncatedWittVector p₁ n R` and `TruncatedWittVector p₂ n R` are definitionally
equal as types but will have different ring operations.)
-/
@[nolint unusedArguments]
def TruncatedWittVector (_ : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (R : Type*) :=
  Fin n → R

section

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p]

/-- `PerfectClosure.R` is the relation `(n, x) ∼ (n + 1, x ^ p)` for `n : ℕ` and `x : K`.
`PerfectClosure K p` is the quotient by this relation. -/
@[mk_iff]
inductive PerfectClosure.R : ℕ × K → ℕ × K → Prop
  | intro : ∀ n x, PerfectClosure.R (n, x) (n + 1, frobenius K p x)

/-- The perfect closure is the smallest extension that makes frobenius surjective. -/
def PerfectClosure : Type u :=
  Quot (PerfectClosure.R K p)

-- morphism levels before object levels. See note [category theory universes].
/-- The core of a category C is the groupoid whose morphisms are all the
isomorphisms of C. -/
structure Core (C : Type u₁) where
  /-- The object of the base category underlying an object in `Core C`. -/
  of : C

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C]

/-- The hom-type between two objects of `Core C`.
It is defined as a one-field structure to prevent defeq abuses. -/
@[ext]
structure CoreHom (X Y : Core C) where
  /-- The isomorphism of objects of `C` underlying a morphism in `Core C`. -/
  iso : X.of ≅ Y.of

@[simps! id_iso inv_iso]
instance coreCategory : Groupoid.{v₁} (Core C) where
  Hom (X Y : Core C) := CoreHom X Y
  id (X : Core C) := .mk <| Iso.refl X.of
  comp f g := .mk <| Iso.trans f.iso g.iso
  inv {_ _} f := .mk <| Iso.symm f.iso

/-- The fppf precoverage on the category of schemes. The covering families are jointly-surjective
families of flat morphisms, locally of finite presentation. -/
def fppfPrecoverage : Precoverage Scheme.{u} :=
  precoverage (@Flat ⊓ @LocallyOfFinitePresentation)
  deriving Precoverage.IsStableUnderBaseChange, Precoverage.IsStableUnderComposition

lemma zariskiPrecoverage_le_fppfPrecoverage :
    zariskiPrecoverage ≤ fppfPrecoverage :=
  precoverage_mono fun _ _ _ _ ↦ ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

lemma fppfPrecoverage_eq_inf :
    fppfPrecoverage = precoverage @Flat ⊓ precoverage @LocallyOfFinitePresentation := by
  grind [fppfPrecoverage, precoverage, precoverage, MorphismProperty.precoverage_inf]

/-- The fppf topology on the category of schemes is topology generated by the fppf precoverage. -/
abbrev fppfTopology : GrothendieckTopology Scheme.{u} :=
  fppfPrecoverage.toGrothendieck

noncomputable def pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor :
    HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor (R := k) (H := H) ⋙ GrpCat.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅
  tensorAutFunctor k H :=
  NatIso.ofComponents
    (fun A ↦ (MulEquiv.ulift.trans (fgPointTensorIsoEquiv k H A)).toGrpIso.trans
      (eqToIso (tensorAutFunctor_obj k H A).symm))
    (fun {A B} φ ↦ by
      apply (cancel_mono (eqToHom (tensorAutFunctor_obj k H B))).mp
      refine GrpCat.hom_ext (MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_)
      -- Both sides of the naturality square are, once evaluated, plain group-element
      -- equations. Reaching them by rewriting is not possible: the two composites are
      -- wrapped in the composite functor `pointsFunctor ⋙ uliftFunctor`, the universe lift's
      -- conjugation by `MulEquiv.ulift`, and `MulEquiv.toGrpIso`, none of which has a
      -- rewriting lemma for an application. All three reduce definitionally, so `change`
      -- states the evaluated square once, explicitly, and the two named lemmas finish.
      change fgPointTensorIsoEquiv k H B (AlgHom.mapValue φ.hom x.down) =
        eqToHom (tensorAutFunctor_obj k H B)
          ((tensorAutFunctor k H).map φ
            (eqToHom (tensorAutFunctor_obj k H A).symm
              (fgPointTensorIsoEquiv k H A x.down)))
      rw [tensorAutFunctor_map_transport_apply]
      exact fgPointTensorIsoEquiv_mapValue k H φ x.down)

items.name: Connected reductive group predicate
items.statement: Reuse the field-level predicate: a finite-type commutative Hopf algebra over a field k is reductive when it is smooth and geometrically connected and has no nontrivial connected normal smooth unipotent subgroup after base change to an algebraic closure. The paper uses reductive groups over the field Q_p (§0.3, p. 409), but mainly reductive group schemes over O (and over Z_p, O_E): smooth affine group schemes over the base whose geometric fibres satisfy this predicate (§0.2 p. 407; Theorem 1.4 p. 415; §2 p. 429; §3.1 p. 455; §3.2 p. 460). The pinned declaration (TauCeti.reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty, over [Field k]) supplies only the fibre condition. The relative notion over O is not pinned; see missing item reductive-group-scheme-over-O.

items.name: Ordinary unbounded derived category
items.statement: For an abelian category C with a chosen localization (HasDerivedCategory), DerivedCategory C is the category of ℤ-indexed cochain complexes localized at quasi-isomorphisms. The paper does not use this unbounded category directly. It uses the bounded constructible ℓ-adic derived categories D^b_c(X, Q̄_ℓ) of separated pfp perfect algebraic spaces, defined 'as usual' through a finite-type model (A.3.1, p. 478), and their equivariant versions (A.3.5; §2.1). The pinned carrier only supplies the finite-coefficient derived categories of étale sheaves underlying that formalism.

items.name: Tor bifunctor
items.statement: In an abelian monoidal preadditive category with projective resolutions, Tor C n is the left derived functor of tensoring in the second factor, and higher Tor vanishes when the second argument is projective. The paper uses only Tor_1 over the ring W(R), R perfect, in the proof of Lemma 1.14 (p. 422). For a W(R)/p-module Q it uses the exact sequence 0 → Tor^{W(R)}(Q, W(R)/p) → F/p → x*E/p → Q → 0 and the canonical isomorphism (1.3.2) Q = Tor^{W(R)}(Q, W(R)/p). That isomorphism comes from the free resolution W(R) --p--> W(R) of W(R)/p, which needs p to be a non-zero-divisor in W(R).

items.name: Finite subcomodule containing a finite subspace
items.statement: Over a field k, for a coalgebra C and a C-comodule M, every finite-dimensional k-subspace P lies in a finite-dimensional subcomodule.

items.name: Tannaka comparison for a known Hopf algebra

items.name: Weakly normal model with prescribed generic fields
items.statement: Let X be a pfp perfect algebraic space over k with generic points eta_1,...,eta_n, and for each i let K_i in k(eta_i) be a subfield finitely generated over k whose perfection is k(eta_i). items.name: Ramified Witt coefficients
items.statement: Fix a perfect field k of characteristic p > 0 and write O_0 = W(k), F_0 = W(k)[1/p]. Except in §3.2, F is a totally ramified finite extension of F_0, O is its ring of integers and ϖ a uniformizer of O. Equivalently, O is a complete DVR of characteristic 0 with residue field k, via the canonical map W(k) → O. For a perfect k-algebra R put W_O(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(k)} O and W_{O,n}(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(k)} O/ϖ^n (= W_O(R)/ϖ^n). W_O(R) is ϖ-adically complete; the paper does not state this, but it is implicit in L^+ = lim L^h.

items.name: Witt lattices and relative position
items.statement: §1.2 (G = GL_n, F = F_0, Gr := Gr_{GL_n}). For a perfect k-algebra R, GL_n-torsors on D_R = Spec W(R) are identified with finite projective W(R)-modules, and Gr(R) = {(𝓔, β) : 𝓔 a rank n projective W(R)-module, β : 𝓔[1/p] ≅ 𝓔_0[1/p] = W(R)[1/p]^n}. Equivalently, 𝓔 is a lattice in W(R)[1/p]^n as in (0.1.2). A quasi-isogeny β : 𝓔_1 ⇢ 𝓔_2 of finite projective W(R)-modules is an isomorphism 𝓔_1[1/p] ≅ 𝓔_2[1/p]. It is an isogeny if it extends to a map 𝓔_1 → 𝓔_2. For a perfect field k and a quasi-isogeny β : E_1 ⇢ E_2 of finite projective W(k)-modules, there are bases (e_i) of E_1 and (f_i) of E_2 with β(e_i) = p^{m_i} f_i and m_1 ≥ … ≥ m_n. The sequence is independent of the bases, and Inv(β) := (m_1, …, m_n) ∈ 𝕏_•(D_n)^+ (1.2.1). β is an isogeny iff m_n ≥ 0. For perfect R and x ∈ Spec R, β_x : 𝓔_1 ⊗ W(k(x))[1/p] → 𝓔_2 ⊗ W(k(x))[1/p] is the base change. Put (Spec R)_μ = {x : Inv(β_x) = μ} ⊂ (Spec R)_{≤μ} = {x : Inv(β_x) ≤ μ}. β is of relative position μ if (Spec R)_μ = Spec R.

items.statement: Lemma 1.5. Let R be a perfect k-algebra and β: E1 ⇢ E2 a quasi-isogeny of finite projective W(R)-modules (GL_n over O_0 = W(k), uniformizer p). If β is of relative position ω_i, i.e. (Spec R)_{ω_i} = Spec R with ω_i = (1^i, 0^{n−i}), then β induces a chain of inclusions pE2 ⊂ E1 ⊂ E2 and E2/E1 is a finite projective W(R)/p = R-module of rank i. A similar statement holds for ω_i^* = ω_{n−i} − ω_n: then β^{-1} induces pE1 ⊂ E2 ⊂ E1 with E1/E2 projective of rank i.
proofSteps: Detect integrality fibrewise, use reducedness and constant-rank finite presentation, and lift projectivity over the complete Witt ring. Correct the inverse-map scalar and quotient orientation in sourceIssues.

items.statement: Lemma 1.9. Let M = M_n × G_m, π: M → A^1, π(A,t) = t·det A, i_N: Spec Z_p → A^1, u ↦ p^N, and V_N = Spec Z_p ×_{i_N, A^1, π} M. items.name: Finite-jet stabilizer presentation
items.statement: Assume h > N. Greenberg realization of det gives (det_0, …, det_{h−1}): L_p^hM_n = A^{n²h} → L_p^hA^1 = A^h. Set V'_{N,h} = {A ∈ L_p^hM_n : det_0A = … = det_{N−1}A = 0, det_NA ∈ G_m} (1.2.4) and V_{N,h} = (V'_{N,h})^{p^{-∞}}. Let J = {(A,γ) ∈ V_{N,h} × L^hGL_n : Aγ = A} be the stabilizer group scheme of the right L^hGL_n-action (1.2.5). Let \overline{Gr}_{N,h} = L^+V_N/L^+GL_n^{(h)}, the L^hGL_n-torsor over \overline{Gr}_N of triples (E, β, ε̄) with ε̄: E_0|_{W_h(R)} ≅ E|_{W_h(R)}. Lemma 1.10: there is an isomorphism J ≅ \overline{Gr}_{N,h}; in particular \overline{Gr}_{N,h} is represented by a perfect affine scheme, perfectly of finite type. Remark 1.11: the isomorphism depends on a lifting of L^+V_N → V_{N,h}; the paper fixes the Teichmüller-digit lifting W_h(R) → W(R), Σ_{0≤i<h} p^i[r_i] mod p^h ↦ Σ_{0≤i<h} p^i[r_i].

items.name: Weil-restriction comparison
items.statement: §1.4.1, p. 426. If O is a totally ramified finite extension of O_0 = W(k) and G is an affine group scheme over O, then Gr_G ≅ Gr_{Res_{O/O_0}G}, where the Weil restriction Res_{O/O_0}G is a group scheme over O_0. proofSteps: Apply the defining functorial property of Weil restriction. A ramified integral restriction need not be reductive; use the parahoric argument separately.

items.name: Hyperbolic localization
items.statement: Braden's hyperbolic localization for algebraic spaces [DG14]. For a G_m-action on a finite-type model with fixed-point component Z, attracting locus p^+: X^+ → Z (inclusion i^+) and repelling locus p^−: X^− → Z (inclusion i^−), there is a canonical isomorphism (p^+)_!(i^+)^* ≅ (p^−)_*(i^−)^! on G_m-monodromic complexes. The paper applies it to the action of G_m^{p^{-∞}} through 2ρ^∨, with fixed points ϖ^λ, S_λ attracting and S_λ^- repelling. For A ∈ Sat_G this gives (2.2.10): H_c^*(S_λ, A) ≅ H^*_{S_λ^-}(A), the cohomology of the !-restriction to S_λ^-.
items.locator: §2.2.1, (2.2.10), p. 436 (Braden's theorem for algebraic spaces [DG14], applied to a model); not in A.3.1

items.name: Fundamental classes and top components
items.statement: (a) For X irreducible of dimension d, the paper defines a 'canonical' isomorphism c_X : H^{2d}_c(X_kbar, Qlbar(d)) = Qlbar as c_{X'} o (eps^*)^{-1} for a model eps : X -> X' (c_{X'} the trace isomorphism), and claims it is independent of the model (see E26, E27). Alternatively c_X is built from c_{P^{1,p^-inf}} : H^2(P^{1,p^-inf}_kbar, mu_{l^n}) = coker(Pic(P^{1,p^-inf}) --l^n--> Pic(P^{1,p^-inf})) = Z/l^n and the six operations. (b) For X separated pfp, omega_X = f^! Qlbar and H^BM_i(X_kbar) = H^{-i}(X_kbar, omega_X(-i/2)). Perfectly proper f gives f_* on H^BM_*. H^BM_i(X_kbar) = H^i_c(X_kbar, Qlbar(i/2))^*. For X irreducible of dimension d, [X] := c_X in H^BM_{2d}(X_kbar). For X of dimension d with d-dimensional irreducible components X_1..X_n, sum_i H^BM_{2d}((X_i)_kbar) = H^BM_{2d}(X_kbar) and [X] = sum [X_i]. For X irreducible and perfectly smooth, [X] : Qlbar -> omega_X[-2d](-d) is an isomorphism, so H^BM_i(X_kbar) = H^{2d-i}(X_kbar, Qlbar(d-i/2)). (c) For Z closed of codimension r, cl(Z) is the image of [Z] in H^BM_{2(d-r)}(X_kbar); if X is perfectly smooth and perfectly proper, cl(Z) is in H^{2r}(X_kbar, Qlbar(r)).

items.statement: §2.1 (k algebraically closed, G connected reductive over O). The L^+G-action on each Gr_{≤μ} factors through some L^hG, perfectly of finite type, so P_{L^+G}(Gr_{≤μ}) is defined (A.3.5). P_{L^+G}(Gr_G) := lim→_μ P_{L^+G}(Gr_{≤μ}). items.name: Quasi-minuscule parahoric resolution
items.statement: Let μ = θ be quasi-minuscule but not minuscule (so θ is a coroot). For r ∈ [0,1], let Q_r = L^+𝒢_r, where 𝒢_r is the parahoric group scheme of the subgroup of G(F) generated by T(O) and ϖ^{⌈⟨rμ,α⟩⌉}O ⊂ U_α(F) for all roots α. items.name: Longest double-coset involution indexing
items.statement: Let I be the standard Iwahori, W̃ = N_G(T)(F)/T(O) = W_a ⋊ Ω (Ω = the length-zero elements), S the simple affine reflections, 0 ∈ S the vertex of G(O), J = S ∖ {0}, W_J ≅ W̄ with w_J ↦ w_0. Define the involution ∗ of W̃ by w^* = w_J w w_J (w ∈ W_J) and λ^* = −w_0(λ) (λ ∈ X_•); it stabilizes S and fixes s_0. For every ω ∈ Ω, ω^* = ω^{−1} ([LY13, Lemma 6.2], published Lemma 7.2(1)), and w^⋄ := ωw^*ω^{−1} is an involution of W_a stabilizing S. Put I_⋄ = {w ∈ W_a : w^⋄ = w^{−1}} and W_J^⋄ = ωW_Jω^{−1}. The longest element of every (W_J, W_J^⋄)-double coset lies in I_⋄ ([Lus12, Prop. 8.2], [LY13, Th. 6.3(1)] = published Th. 7.3(1)). For μ ∈ X_• with ϖ^μ ∈ W_aω, d_μ is the longest element of W_J(ϖ^μω^{−1})W_J^⋄, and d_λ is defined in the same way for λ ≤ μ.

items.name: Finite-level opposite IC comparison
items.statement: Lemma 2.23: there is an equivalence of monoidal categories Id': Sat^op_G ≃ Sat_G sending IC^op_μ (the IC sheaf of Gr^op_≤μ, the closure of Gr^op_μ = L^+G\L^+Gϖ^μL^+G) to IC_μ. Lemma 2.24: for m with L^+G^(m) ⊂ L^+G ∩ ϖ^μL^+Gϖ^{−μ} and the diagram (2.4.1), there is a unique isomorphism id'_μ: φ_m^*IC^op_μ ≃ π_m^*IC_μ of sheaves on Gr^(m)_≤μ whose restriction to Gr^(m)_μ is the identity of Q̄_ℓ[(2ρ,μ)]. In particular φ_m^*IC^op_μ[m dim G] is perverse. The monoidal structure of Id' comes from the isomorphisms id'_μ• on Sat^{0,op}_G ≃ Sat^0_G.
proofSteps: First prove the comparison on minuscule/quasi-minuscule resolutions, then on products and summands; do not assume the opposite projection smooth.

items.name: Canonical opposite stalk and costalk maps
items.statement: For λ ∈ X_•, let H^j_λ A (resp. H^j_{λ,!}A) be the degree-j stalk (resp. costalk) cohomology of A at ϖ^λ. Corollary 2.26: there is a canonical isomorphism H^j_λ id': H^j_λ A ≃ H^j_λ Id'A for A ∈ P_{L+G}(Gr^op), and similarly for H^j_{λ,!}. For A = IC^op_μ it is H^j_λIC^op_μ = H^j_λφ_m^*IC^op_μ ≃ H^j_λπ_m^*IC_μ = H^j_λIC_μ, which is independent of m; the costalk statement follows by Verdier duality.
proofSteps: Use the common finite-level torsor diagram and Verdier duality. Avoid inferring a shift by moving a bracket through an unspecified dual symbol.

items.name: Normalized IC involution
items.statement: Fix √−1 ∈ Q̄_ℓ and set (−1)^{(ρ,μ)} := √−1^{(2ρ,μ)}. (2.4.2) N_μ: θ^*IC_μ → IC^op_μ is the isomorphism whose restriction to Gr^op_μ is the identity of Q̄_ℓ[(2ρ,μ)]. items.name: Reversal comparison on cohomology
items.statement: Lemma 2.28: there is a canonical isomorphism of functors δ: H^* ≃ H^*∘θ^* (pullback along θ: Gr^op ≃ Gr) such that for all A_1, A_2 ∈ P_{L+G}(Gr) the two composites H^*(A_1⋆A_2) → H^*(θ^*A_2)⊗H^*(θ^*A_1) agree. The first is δ followed by θ^*(A_1⋆A_2) ≃ θ^*A_2⋆θ^*A_1 and Künneth; the second is Künneth, then c_vect, then δ⊗δ. The paper writes c_vect, which Proposition 2.21 defined as the plain flip; for §2.4.4 to be consistent it must here be the Koszul-signed flip a⊗b ↦ (−1)^{|a||b|}b⊗a (see the new issue on p. 449).
proofSteps: Apply the anti-involution to the finite-level convolution correspondence and its Künneth map.

items.name: Closed and exact affine Deligne–Lusztig spaces
items.statement: Setting of §3.1.1: k a (finite) perfect field of characteristic p, F a totally ramified finite extension of F_0 = W(k)[1/p] with ring of integers O and uniformizer ϖ, L the completion of the maximal unramified extension of F, σ ∈ Gal(L/F) the Frobenius, G a reductive group scheme over O. For b ∈ G(L) and μ ∈ X_•^+, the (closed) affine Deligne–Lusztig variety is X_≤μ(b) = {g mod L^+G ∈ Gr_G | g^{-1} b σ(g) ∈ closure of L^+G ϖ^μ L^+G} (3.1.1). As a moduli functor: with E_0 the trivial G-torsor and b : σ^*E_0 → E_0 over the punctured disc, X_≤μ(b)(R) = {(E, β) ∈ Gr_G(R) | Inv_x(β^{-1} b σ(β)) ≤ μ for all x ∈ Spec R} for perfect R (3.1.2) (R should be a k̄-algebra, since b ∈ G(L)). By Lemma 1.22 it is a closed subspace of Gr_G. Replacing '≤' by '=' defines an open subspace X_μ(b) ⊂ X_≤μ(b). With Φ = β^{-1} b σ(β), (E, Φ) is an F-crystal with G-structure on Spec R whose Hodge polygon is bounded by μ (resp. equal to μ).
items.locator: §3.1.1, (3.1.1)–(3.1.2) and the paragraph after them, p. 455

items.name: Basic-Levi reduction
items.statement: (Cited: [GHKR06, Prop. 5.6.1, Th. 5.8.1], adapted.) The Newton point ν_b is defined over F, and its centralizer M in G is an F-rational Levi subgroup. After σ-conjugation, b ∈ M(L), and b is then basic in M. The arguments of [GHKR06] reduce (3.1.3) for (G, b, μ) to (3.1.3) for (M, b, μ_M), for various μ_M. They rely on [GHKR06, Prop. 5.3.1 and 5.4.3]. The proof of 5.3.1 applies unchanged; it uses an M-equivariant isomorphism N ≃ 𝔫 of F-schemes and the p-adic loop space of 𝔫 (§4 of loc. cit.). The proof of 5.4.3 extends using the Lefschetz trace formula for separated pfp perfect algebraic spaces (A.3.4). The same Levi argument applies again when a basic b lies in a proper F-Levi, so it suffices to treat superbasic b.
proofSteps: Read the original reduction and prove the exact dimension comparison; do not assume dimensions are unchanged by the Levi passage.

items.name: Superbasic adjoint reduction
items.statement: (Cited: [GHKR06], [CKV15].) Theorem 3.1 reduces to the case where b is superbasic and G = G_ad is simple of adjoint type. If G is simple of adjoint type (reductive over O, so G_F is unramified) and has a superbasic σ-conjugacy class, then G_F ≅ Res_{E/F} PGL_n for some unramified extension E/F. So it remains to prove Proposition 3.3 (G_F = Res_{E/F} GL_n, b superbasic).
proofSteps: Separate central isogeny, product and superbasic-support reductions and their component conditions; the original classification remains a proof gate.

items.name: M-equivariant isomorphism N ≃ 𝔫 in mixed characteristic (input to the Levi reduction)
items.statement: Let M be the centralizer of ν_b, P = MN the corresponding F-parabolic and 𝔫 = Lie N. In equal characteristic the M-equivariant isomorphism N ≃ 𝔫 used in [GHKR06] makes sense both as F-schemes and as k-ind-schemes. In mixed characteristic it is only an isomorphism of F-schemes. The p-adic loop space L𝔫 still makes sense, so the arguments of [GHKR06, §4] and the proof of [GHKR06, Prop. 5.3.1] apply. items.name: Top-stratum lower bound
items.statement: (Equality step in the proof of Proposition 3.3.) Assume X^H_≤|μ•|((Nm b)σ_E) ≠ ∅, which is equivalent to X^G_≤μ(bσ) ≠ ∅. Over the open stratum Gr_|μ•|, m : Gr_≤μ• → Gr_≤|μ•| is surjective with finite fibres. So the preimage of X^H_|μ•|((Nm b)σ_E) has dimension dim X^H_|μ•|((Nm b)σ_E). By (3.1.3) for H, applied to each λ' < |μ•|, dim X^H_≤λ'(…) ≤ (ρ_H, λ' − ν_{Nm b}) − ½ def_H(Nm b), which is strictly less than (ρ_H, |μ•| − ν_{Nm b}) − ½ def_H(Nm b) because (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ') ≥ 1. Hence dim X^H_|μ•| = dim X^H_≤|μ•| = (ρ_H, |μ•| − ν_{Nm b}) − ½ def_H(Nm b), and the upper bound is attained.

items.name: Affine Deligne–Lusztig dimension theorem
items.statement: Let F be a totally ramified finite extension of F_0 = W(k)[1/p] with ring of integers O, L the completion of the maximal unramified extension of F, σ ∈ Gal(L/F) the Frobenius, G a reductive group scheme over O, b ∈ G(L) and μ ∈ X_•^+ a dominant coweight. The closed affine Deligne–Lusztig space X_≤μ(b) ⊂ Gr_G of (3.1.1)–(3.1.2) and its open stratum X_μ(b) are finite-dimensional. If X_≤μ(b) ≠ ∅, then dim X_≤μ(b) = ⟨ρ, μ − ν_b⟩ − ½ def_G(b) (Theorem 3.1, formula (3.1.3)); if X_μ(b) ≠ ∅, then dim X_μ(b) = ⟨ρ, μ − ν_b⟩ − ½ def_G(b) (Theorem 0.5). Here ν_b is the Newton point of b and def_G(b) = rk_F G − rk_F J_b. The paper prints both formulas without the nonemptiness hypothesis (see E19).
proofSteps: Combine the reductions. The nonempty qualification is essential; no empty-set dimension convention turns the torus mismatch into the printed finite value.

items.name: Contravariant Dieudonné module over perfect rings
items.statement: For R ∈ Nilp_W and a p-divisible group X over Spec R, D(X) is its contravariant Dieudonné crystal. It is an F-crystal on Spec R: a locally free crystal on the big crystalline site CRIS(R/W) with Frobenius F : σ^*D(X) → D(X), for which there is V : D(X) → σ^*D(X) with VF = p^i (i = 1 for p-divisible groups). The value D(X)_R at the trivial thickening carries the Hodge filtration Fil^0 = D(X)_R ⊃ Fil^1 = (Lie X)^* ⊃ Fil^2 = 0, with locally free graded pieces; D(X)^⊗ inherits F (after inverting p) and a filtration. Over k = F̄_p, D(X_0) is the classical contravariant Dieudonné module with (F, V). Over a perfect F̄_p-algebra R, a crystal is a finite projective W(R)-module (p. 463).
items.locator: §3.2, p. 461 (contravariant Dieudonné module and crystal, Hodge filtration); proof of Proposition 3.11, p. 463

items.name: Hodge-type framed datum
items.statement: (k = F̄_p, W = W(k), L = W[1/p].) The data are: a reductive group G over Z_p; a geometric conjugacy class of cocharacters μ : G_m → G, with a fixed representative; a σ-conjugacy class of b ∈ G(L) with a representative b ∈ G(W) p^μ G(W); and a free Z_p-lattice Λ with a faithful representation ρ : G → GL(Λ) such that ρμ has weights 0, 1 on Λ ⊗ W. Write Λ ⊗ W = Λ^0 ⊕ Λ^1 for the weight decomposition and Fil^0 = Λ ⊗ W ⊃ Fil^1 = Λ^1 for the induced filtration. Put rk Λ^1 = n and rk Λ = h (equivalently ρμ is the n-th fundamental coweight). Choose finitely many tensors s_i ∈ Λ^⊗ (the tensor algebra of Λ ⊕ Λ^*) with G = Aut(Λ, {s_i}), and let P_μ = Aut(Λ, {s_i}, Fil^•(Λ ⊗ W)), a parabolic subgroup of G_W. The framing: the paper asserts that there is a p-divisible group X_0 over F̄_p of dimension n and height h with ε : D(X_0) ≃ Λ ⊗_{Z_p} W such that (1) εF = ρ(b)(id_Λ ⊗ σ)ε and (2) ε((Lie X_0)^*) = Fil^1 Λ ⊗ F̄_p, unique up to unique isomorphism. Condition (2) needs an adapted representative b and a Q_p-rational class {μ}; see E21 and the new σ-twist issue.

items.statement: (Proof of Proposition 3.11, case (G, b, μ) = (GL_h, b, ω_n), ρ = id.) There is an isomorphism X_{ω_n}(b) ≃ M̄^{p^{-∞}}, where M̄ is the special fibre of M_{X_0} (= M(GL_h, b, ω_n) by Theorem 3.10(2)). No hypothesis p > 2 is needed here. By Lemma 1.5, F is regular with D/F(σ^*D) locally free of rank n, and V = pF^{-1} is regular. Gabber's theorem then gives (X, ι) with D(X) = D and D(ι) = β. Conversely, (X, ι) goes to E = Isom(D(X), Λ ⊗ W(R)) with the quasi-isogeny β : E ⇢ E_0 induced by ι, and Inv_x(F) ≤ ω_n.
proofSteps: Translate a minuscule lattice into integral F and V=pF⁻¹, recover the p-divisible group through the perfect-ring equivalence, and check the quasi-isogeny direction.
