items.name: Witt vectors of a perfect ring
items.statement: Let R be a perfect ring of characteristic p (in the paper, a perfect k-algebra). Then p is a non-zero-divisor in W(R), W(R) is p-adically complete and separated, and W(R)/p^h W(R) ≅ W_h(R) for every h ≥ 1; in particular W(R)/p ≅ R. For nonreduced R, p can be a zero divisor in W(R), so W(R)^n need not embed in W(R)[1/p]^n.
items.locator: §0.1.3, p. 405 ('p could be a zero divisor of W(R) if R is nonreduced'; '(1) if R is a perfect k-algebra, then W(R) is well behaved'); §0.5, p. 411 ('If R is perfect, W_h(R) = W(R)/p^hW(R)')
items.note: This standard fact is stated as notation and used throughout §1: identifying lattices with finite projective W(R)-modules, Lemma 1.10 (p. 420), Remark 1.11 (p. 421) and (1.3.2) (p. 422). At the pinned Mathlib (082e2d3), Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Complete.lean has WittVector.eq_zero_of_p_mul_eq_zero, WittVector.mem_span_p_pow_iff_le_coeff_eq_zero and isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP (checked by the review). The nonreduced example: for x with x^p = 0, p·[x] = V([x^p]) = 0. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Teichmüller lift and Teichmüller expansions
items.statement: For a k-algebra R, the Teichmüller lift R → W(R), x ↦ [x] = (x, 0, 0, …), is multiplicative. When R is perfect, every element of W(R) can be written uniquely as Σ_{i≥0} p^i [r_i] with r_i ∈ R, and every element of W_h(R) = W(R)/p^h uniquely as Σ_{0≤i<h} p^i [r_i].
items.note: Remark 1.11 (p. 421) uses the expansion to fix the lifting W_h(R) → W(R), Σ_{i<h} p^i[r_i] mod p^h ↦ Σ_{i<h} p^i[r_i], on which the isomorphism of Lemma 1.10 depends; Appendix B.3 (p. 486) also uses it. In Mathlib: WittVector.teichmuller (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Teichmuller.lean) and the expansion lemmas in TeichmullerSeries.lean. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: O_L, L and the families of discs D_{F,R}, D*_{F,R}
items.statement: Put O_L := W_O(k̄) and L := O_L[1/p]; L is the completion of the maximal unramified extension of F. For a perfect k-algebra R set D_{F,R} := Spec W_O(R) and D*_{F,R} := Spec W_O(R)[1/p], a family of discs (resp. punctured discs) parametrized by Spec R. The subscript F is omitted when F = F_0 and the subscript R when R = k.
items.note: Used in §1.1 (G-torsors on D_{F,R} trivialized over D*_{F,R}), in §3.1 (p. 455: the trivial torsor E_0 on D_F = Spec O and b : σ*E_0|_{D*_F} → E_0|_{D*_F}) and throughout §§2–3 (L, O_L). G01 covers only W_O(R). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Reductive group schemes over O and the standing group hypothesis
items.statement: A (connected) reductive group scheme G over O (likewise over Z_p or O_E) is a smooth affine group scheme over the base whose geometric fibres are connected reductive groups. Standing convention: unless otherwise stated, G is a smooth affine group scheme over O with connected geometric fibres, and E_0 is the trivial G-torsor.
items.locator: §0.5, p. 412 (standing hypothesis); reductive group schemes over O are used in §0.2 p. 407, §0.3 p. 409, Theorem 1.4 p. 415, §2 p. 429, §3.1 p. 455 and §3.2 p. 460
items.note: L06 pins only the field-level predicate; the relative notion, which is what every main theorem assumes, has no item. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Split reductive data, coweight lattice, dominance order and ϖ^λ
items.statement: When G is a split reductive group over O, choose a Borel subgroup B ⊂ G over O and a split maximal torus T ⊂ B; U ⊂ B is the unipotent radical, and Ḡ, B̄, Ū, T̄ are the reductions modulo ϖ. X_• is the coweight lattice of T, X^• the weight lattice and X_•^+ the semigroup of coweights dominant for B. 2ρ ∈ X^• is the sum of the positive roots. On X_•, λ ≤ μ means that μ − λ is a Z_{≥0}-combination of positive coroots (the paper prints 'roots'; see E2). For λ ∈ X_•, ϖ^λ is the image of ϖ ∈ F^× = G_m(F) under λ : G_m → T → G.
items.note: Used in §§1.4, 2 and 3 (Gr_μ, Gr_≤μ, S_λ, (2ρ, μ), ⟨ρ, μ − ν_b⟩). L08/L09 give the lattices only for abstract tori, not the dominance order or ϖ^λ. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Dual group Ĝ, B̂, T̂ and the modules V_μ, V_μ(λ)
items.statement: Ĝ is the (Langlands) dual group of G over a field of characteristic 0 (in the paper Q̄_ℓ), equipped with a dual Borel B̂ and a maximal torus T̂ dual to T, so that X^•(T̂) = X_•(T). For μ ∈ X_•^+, V_μ is the irreducible representation of Ĝ of highest weight μ. For λ ∈ X_•, V_μ(λ) is the λ-weight subspace of V_μ.
items.locator: §0.5, p. 412 (footnote 11: the Tannakian group from the geometric Satake comes with B̂ and T̂)
items.note: Used in Theorem 0.3 (p. 408), in the weight-multiplicity statements of §2.2 and in the identification with the dual group in §2.5 (T06/T07), where the dual group is used but never defined. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Equal-characteristic affine Grassmannian Gr^♭ and its bounded pieces
items.statement: For a k-algebra R, a lattice in R((t))^n is a finitely generated projective R[[t]]-submodule Λ ⊂ R((t))^n with Λ ⊗_{R[[t]]} R((t)) = R((t))^n. Gr^♭(R) is the set of such lattices, and Gr^♭(k) = GL_n(k((t)))/GL_n(k[[t]]). Every lattice satisfies t^N R[[t]]^n ⊂ Λ ⊂ t^{−N} R[[t]]^n for some N (0.1.1). Gr^{♭,(N)} is the subfunctor of lattices satisfying (0.1.1), and Gr^♭ = ∪_N Gr^{♭,(N)}. The map Λ ↦ t^{−N}R[[t]]^n/Λ identifies Gr^{♭,(N)}(R) with the set of quotient R[[t]]-modules of t^{−N}R[[t]]^n/t^N R[[t]]^n that are projective as R-modules, so Gr^{♭,(N)} is represented by a closed subscheme of a usual Grassmannian (classical; [BL94]).
items.note: Used later as the equal-characteristic comparison object: p. 423 (Gr^♭ analogue of Gr_{μ•}), p. 441 (monoidal structure via Gr^♭), pp. 482 and 484 (Appendix B), and implicitly in the [LY13] and [Vie06] inputs. No existing item defines it. Missing: routed to route 10.

items.name: Equal-characteristic determinant line bundle L^♭_det
items.statement: On Gr̄^♭_N (lattices Λ ⊂ R[[t]]^n with ∧^nΛ = t^N ∧^n R[[t]]^n), the determinant line bundle L^♭_det has as fibre at Λ the top exterior power over R of the rank-N projective R-module R[[t]]^n/Λ.
items.note: Recalled on p. 482 (Appendix B.1) as the model for the mixed-characteristic determinant line bundle. The intro only says the construction 'certainly fails in mixed characteristic'. Missing: routed to route 10.

items.name: Gabber's Dieudonné theory over perfect rings (cited)
items.statement: (Gabber; see [Lau13, §6].) Let R be a perfect ring of characteristic p > 0. The contravariant Dieudonné module functor X ↦ D(X) is an anti-equivalence between p-divisible groups over R and Dieudonné modules over W(R): finite projective W(R)-modules D with a σ-linear F : D → D and a σ^{-1}-linear V : D → D such that FV = VF = p. It is compatible with quasi-isogenies. In particular, for any such (D, F, V) there is a p-divisible group X over Spec R with D(X) ≅ D.
items.locator: §0.3, p. 410 (cited: 'the equivalence of categories between p-divisible groups and F-crystals over a perfect ring in characteristic p > 0 (a theorem of Gabber; see also [Lau13, §6])'); used in the proof of Proposition 3.11, p. 463
items.note: A black-box result from another paper, and the key input of Proposition 0.4 / 3.11. E's R01 mentions it only inside a definition, and there is no theorem item for it. Missing: routed to route 16.

items.name: Standing assumption on G; coweights, dominance order, ϖ^λ, dual group, V_μ
items.statement: Unless otherwise stated, G is a smooth affine group scheme over 𝒪 with connected geometric fibres, and 𝓔_0 is the trivial G-torsor. When G is split reductive, fix a Borel B ⊂ G over 𝒪 and a split maximal torus T ⊂ B. U is the unipotent radical of B, and Ḡ, B̄, Ū, T̄ are the reductions mod ϖ. 𝕏_• is the coweight lattice of T, 𝕏^• the weight lattice, and 𝕏_•^+ the dominant coweights with respect to B. 2ρ ∈ 𝕏^• is the sum of the positive roots. The partial order on 𝕏_• is λ ≤ μ iff μ − λ is a ℤ_{≥0}-combination of positive coroots (printed: roots; see E2). ϖ^λ is the image of ϖ ∈ F^× = 𝔾_m(F) under λ : 𝔾_m → T → G. Ĝ is the dual group over a field of characteristic 0, with a Borel B̂ and a maximal torus T̂ dual to T. For μ ∈ 𝕏_•^+, V_μ is the irreducible Ĝ-representation of highest weight μ, and V_μ(λ) is its λ-weight space.
items.note: These conventions are used throughout §1–§3. E2 concerns the order. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Greenberg realization (cited black box)
items.statement: [Gre61] For a finite type 𝒪-scheme 𝒳, the presheaves L_p^+𝒳(R) = 𝒳(W_𝒪(R)) and L_p^h𝒳(R) = 𝒳(W_{𝒪,h}(R)) on affine k-schemes are represented by k-schemes. L_p^h𝒳 is of finite type over k, and L_p^+𝒳 = lim← L_p^h𝒳. If 𝒳 ⊂ 𝒴 is open, then L_p^+𝒳 ⊂ L_p^+𝒴 is open.
items.note: Cited from M. J. Greenberg, Schemata over local rings, Ann. of Math. 73 (1961). G02 records the definitions but not this representability result. On non-perfect R the rings must be read as Greenberg's truncated-Witt-vector rings (see the new source issue on §1.1.1). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.5 (relative position ω_i gives a lattice chain)
items.statement: Let R be a perfect k-algebra and β : 𝓔_1 ⇢ 𝓔_2 a quasi-isogeny of finite projective W(R)-modules. If β is of relative position ω_i, then β induces a chain of inclusions p𝓔_2 ⊂ 𝓔_1 ⊂ 𝓔_2, and 𝓔_2/𝓔_1 is a finite projective W(R)/p = R-module of rank i. Similarly, if β is of relative position ω_i^*, then β^{-1} induces p𝓔_1 ⊂ 𝓔_2 ⊂ 𝓔_1, with 𝓔_1/𝓔_2 finite projective over R of rank i.
items.note: The first step of the proof is reused later: a quasi-isogeny that is a genuine map at every point x ∈ Spec R is a genuine map. The proof contains E4, E5 and the noetherian-reduction gap reported below. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.6 (semicontinuity of relative position; cited)
items.statement: For a quasi-isogeny β : 𝓔_1 ⇢ 𝓔_2 of finite projective W(R)-modules over a perfect k-algebra R, (Spec R)_{≤μ} is closed in Spec R, and (Spec R)_μ is open in (Spec R)_{≤μ}. In particular, (Spec R)_{ω_0} is closed.
items.note: Cited as a basic fact from [Kat79, §2.3] (Katz, Slope filtration of F-crystals, Astérisque 63). The paper does not prove it. An elementary proof uses minors: the sum of the j smallest m_i at x is the minimal p-adic valuation of the j×j minors, which is upper semicontinuous, and the total sum is locally constant. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Corollary 1.7 (Gr_{GL_n} has closed diagonal)
items.statement: The diagonal map Δ : Gr → Gr × Gr of Gr = Gr_{GL_n} is a closed embedding. Given (𝓔, β), (𝓔′, β′) over Spec R, the fibre product Spec R ×_{Gr×Gr,Δ} Gr is represented by (Spec R)_{ω_0} for the quasi-isogeny (β′)^{-1}β : 𝓔 ⇢ 𝓔′.
items.note: Used for the separatedness in Proposition 1.12. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: 𝕏_•(D_n)^+, ω_i, ω_i^* and the GL_n dominance order
items.statement: 𝕏_•(D_n)^+ = {(m_1, …, m_n) ∈ ℤ^n : m_1 ≥ … ≥ m_n}, identified with the dominant coweights of GL_n. For 0 ≤ i ≤ n, ω_i = (1, …, 1, 0, …, 0) with i ones, and ω_i^* = ω_{n−i} − ω_n. Over a perfect field, Inv(β) = ω_i iff β extends to a map E_1 → E_2 with pE_2 ⊂ E_1 and dim E_2/E_1 = i. Inv(β) = ω_i^* iff β^{-1} induces pE_1 ⊂ E_2 ⊂ E_1 with dim E_1/E_2 = i. The order is (m_i) ≤ (l_i) iff m_1 + … + m_j ≤ l_1 + … + l_j for j = 1, …, n, with equality for j = n. ω_0 is a minimal element.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Gr_{≤μ} and Gr_μ for GL_n
items.statement: For μ ∈ 𝕏_•(D_n)^+, Gr_{≤μ}(R) = {(𝓔, β) ∈ Gr(R) : (Spec R)_{≤μ} = Spec R}, with the relative position taken for β : 𝓔 ⇢ 𝓔_0. If λ ≤ μ, then Gr_{≤λ} ⊂ Gr_{≤μ} is a closed embedding (Lemma 1.6). Gr_μ = Gr_{≤μ} − ∪_{λ<μ} Gr_{≤λ} is an open subspace of Gr_{≤μ}.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The lattice Λ_μ and the point p^μ
items.statement: (1.2.3) For μ = (m_1, …, m_n) ∈ 𝕏_•(D_n)^+, Λ_μ = W(k){p^{m_1}e_1, …, p^{m_n}e_n} ⊂ W(k)[1/p]^n is the lattice generated by the p^{m_i}e_i. It defines a k-point of Gr, denoted p^μ.
items.note: Used in Lemma 1.8 and Lemma 1.18. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.8 (Cartan decomposition for Gr_{GL_n})
items.statement: (i) The group GL_n(W(k)) acts transitively on Gr_μ(k). In fact, Gr_μ(k) = GL_n(W(k))p^μ. (ii) Gr(k) = ⊔_{μ∈𝕏_•(D_n)^+} Gr_μ(k).
items.note: A reformulation of the elementary divisor theorem. It is stated over the base field k but is used over arbitrary perfect (algebraically closed) fields in Lemma 1.18. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Gr̄_N, Gr_N and the reduction to Gr̄_N
items.statement: Gr̄_N := Gr_{≤Nω_1} and Gr_N := Gr_{Nω_1}. LGL_n acts on Gr, and every Gr_{≤λ} is a closed subspace of g·Gr̄_N for some g ∈ GL_n(F) and N ≫ 0, so representability of Gr reduces to that of Gr̄_N. For perfect R, Gr̄_N(R) = {(𝓔, β) : 𝓔 a rank n projective W(R)-module, β : 𝓔 → 𝓔_0 an isogeny inducing ∧^nβ : ∧^n𝓔 ≅ p^N W(R) ⊂ ∧^n𝓔_0}.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The scheme V_N and Lemma 1.9
items.statement: Let M_n be the scheme of n×n matrices. Let π : M := M_n × 𝔾_m → 𝔸^1, π(A, t) = t det A, and i_N : Spec ℤ_p → 𝔸^1 = Spec ℤ_p[u], u ↦ p^N. Put V_N := ℤ_p ×_{i_N,𝔸^1,π} M, a finite type ℤ_p-scheme with L_p^+V_N(R) = {(A, t) : A ∈ M_n(W(R)), t ∈ W(R)^×, t det A = p^N}. L_p^+GL_n acts on L_p^+V_N by left and right multiplication, and both actions become free after perfection. Lemma 1.9: there is a canonical isomorphism L^+V_N / L^+GL_n = Gr̄_N.
items.note: Proved 'by the same proof of Lemma 1.3', so it inherits the fpqc/étale gap reported below. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The L^hGL_n-torsor Gr̄_{N,h}
items.statement: Gr̄_{N,h} := L^+V_N / L^+GL_n^{(h)}, where L^+GL_n^{(h)} = ker(L^+GL_n → L^hGL_n). In moduli terms, Gr̄_{N,h}(R) = {(𝓔, β, ε̄) : (𝓔, β) ∈ Gr̄_N(R), ε̄ : 𝓔_0|_{W_h(R)} ≅ 𝓔|_{W_h(R)}}. It is an L^hGL_n-torsor over Gr̄_N, with L^hGL_n acting by changing ε̄.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: V′_{N,h}, V_{N,h}, the stabilizer J and the map Gr̄_{N,h} → V_{N,h}
items.statement: For h > N, let (det_0, …, det_{h−1}) : L_p^hM_n = 𝔸^{n²h} → L_p^h𝔸^1 = 𝔸^h be the Greenberg realization of det. (1.2.4) V′_{N,h} := {A ∈ L_p^hM_n : det_0A = … = det_{N−1}A = 0, det_NA ∈ 𝔾_m} and V_{N,h} := (V′_{N,h})^{p^{-∞}}, with the left and right multiplication action of L^hGL_n × L^hGL_n. (1.2.5) J = {(A, γ) ∈ V_{N,h} × L^hGL_n : Aγ = A} is the stabilizer group scheme over V_{N,h} for right multiplication, i.e. the fibre product of Δ : V_{N,h} → V_{N,h} × V_{N,h}. J′ is the analogous stabilizer over V′_{N,h}; it is affine of finite type, and J = (J′)^{p^{-∞}}. The natural map Gr̄_{N,h} → V_{N,h} is (𝓔, β, ε̄) ↦ (β|_{W_h(R)})ε̄.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.10 (Gr̄_{N,h} is affine)
items.statement: Assume h > N. There is an isomorphism J ≅ Gr̄_{N,h}. In particular, Gr̄_{N,h} is represented by a perfect affine scheme, perfectly of finite type.
items.note: The isomorphism depends on a section of L^+V_N → V_{N,h}, which Remark 1.11 fixes. The proof contains E6 and the ε/ε̄ slip below. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Remark 1.11 (normalized lifting)
items.statement: The isomorphism of Lemma 1.10 depends on a choice of lifting of the projection L^+V_N → V_{N,h}. The paper fixes the lifting induced entrywise by W_h(R) → W(R), (Σ_{0≤i<h} p^i[r_i] mod p^h) ↦ Σ_{0≤i<h} p^i[r_i], with t then determined by t det Ã = p^N.
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Proposition 1.12 (representability of Gr̄_N and Gr)
items.statement: The functor Gr̄_N is represented by a separated perfect algebraic space, perfectly of finite type over k. In particular, Gr is representable.
items.note: Proof: apply Theorem A.29 (appendix black box) to the free action of L^hGL_n = (L_p^hGL_n)^{p^{-∞}} on Gr̄_{N,h}. The closedness of L^hGL_n × Gr̄_{N,h} → Gr̄_{N,h} × Gr̄_{N,h} comes from Corollary 1.7. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Proposition 1.13 (Gr_{μ•} is perfectly proper)
items.statement: For μ_• = (μ_1, …, μ_N) with μ_i ∈ {ω_1, …, ω_n, ω_1^*, …, ω_n^*}, the space Gr_{μ•} is represented by a perfect k-scheme, perfectly proper over k. By the proof, Gr_{ω_i} ≅ Gr^{p^{-∞}}(i, n). Moreover Gr_{μ•,μ_{N+1}} ≅ Gr^{p^{-∞}}(i, 𝓔_N/p) if μ_{N+1} = ω_i, and ≅ Gr^{p^{-∞}}(i, (𝓔_N/p)^*) if μ_{N+1} = ω_i^*, so Gr_{μ•} is an iterated perfected Grassmannian bundle and in fact perfectly projective.
items.note: The proof contains the misprints recorded below on p. 423. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Values x^*𝓔 and 𝓔/p of a locally free crystal
items.statement: Let X be a perfect k-scheme and 𝓔 a rank n locally free crystal on X. For R perfect and x ∈ X(R), x^*𝓔 is the value of 𝓔 on the universal PD thickening W(R) → R, a finite projective W(R)-module of rank n, and x^*𝓔/p is its value on the trivial thickening R → R. These glue to a rank n vector bundle 𝓔/p on X. (p. 415: a finite projective W(R)-module is the same as a finite rank locally free crystal on Spec R.)
items.note: Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.14 (sublattices with rank-i quotient form a Grassmannian bundle)
items.statement: Let X be a perfect k-scheme and 𝓔 a locally free crystal of rank n on X. Let Y be the perfect space over X that assigns to every x : Spec R → X the set of isogenies 𝓕_x → x^*𝓔 of finite projective W(R)-modules such that x^*𝓔/𝓕_x is a locally free W(R)/p-module of rank i. Then Y is represented by the perfect scheme Gr^{p^{-∞}}(i, 𝓔/p) of rank-i quotients of 𝓔/p (introduced in Corollary A.23).
items.note: The proof contains E7. Corollary A.23 is stated for pfp bases, but the lemma allows any perfect X and is applied over arbitrary Spec R in Lemma 1.17. The perfected relative Grassmannian exists over any base, so this is harmless. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Sum of coweights and the map π : Gr_{μ•} → Gr_{≤|μ•|}
items.statement: For λ_1 = (m_i) and λ_2 = (l_i), λ_1 + λ_2 = (m_i + l_i), the usual addition of dominant coweights of GL_n. For μ_• with μ_i ∈ {ω_1, …, ω_n, ω_1^*, …, ω_n^*}, let |μ_•| = Σ μ_i. The natural map (1.3.3) is π : Gr_{μ•} → Gr_{≤|μ•|}, (𝓔_•, β_•) ↦ (𝓔_N, β_1⋯β_N).
items.note: Well-definedness uses the pointwise inequality Inv(β_1⋯β_N) ≤ Σ Inv(β_i). This is a standard elementary-divisor fact, but the paper does not state it. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.17 (π is representable and perfectly proper)
items.statement: The morphism π : Gr_{μ•} → Gr_{≤|μ•|} is representable. It is perfectly proper, and its fibres are perfectly proper perfect schemes.
items.note: The proof contains E8. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The Demazure resolution G̃r_N → Gr̄_N
items.statement: Take μ_i = ω_1 for all i = 1, …, N and write G̃r_N := Gr_{μ•}. It classifies chains (1.3.1) in which all β_i are isogenies and all 𝓔_{i−1}/𝓔_i are invertible W(R)/p-modules. The map (1.3.3) specializes to π : G̃r_N → Gr̄_N (printed as (1.4.2), see E9).
items.note: Remark 1.15 on p. 423 already uses G̃r_1 and G̃r_2 before this definition. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Lemma 1.18 (fibres of the Demazure map)
items.statement: The restriction π^{-1}Gr_N → Gr_N of the map π : G̃r_N → Gr̄_N is an isomorphism. The fibre of π over every point x ∈ Gr̄_N − Gr_N is nonempty, geometrically connected, and of positive dimension.
items.note: The proof uses the factorization (1.3.4) G̃r_N → ℙ^{p^{-∞}}(𝓔/p) → Gr̄_N. It contains the ∩/+ misprint reported below. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Corollary 1.19 (Gr̄_N irreducible and perfectly proper)
items.statement: The separated pfp perfect algebraic space Gr̄_N is irreducible and perfectly proper. In particular, Gr = Gr_{GL_n} is ind-perfectly proper.
items.note: No proof is written. It follows because G̃r_N is an iterated ℙ^{n−1,p^{-∞}}-bundle, hence irreducible and perfectly proper, and π is perfectly proper and surjective (Lemmas 1.17, 1.18). Together with Proposition 1.20 this gives Theorem 1.4 for reductive G. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Relative position and spherical Schubert varieties for split reductive G
items.statement: Let G be split reductive over O (B ⊃ T as in §0.5). For G-torsors E1, E2 over D_{F,K} (K a perfect field over k) and an isomorphism β: E1|_{D*_{F,K}} ≃ E2|_{D*_{F,K}}, the relative position Inv(β) ∈ X_•^+ is defined as in (1.2.1), via the Cartan decomposition. In families, Inv_x(β) is the relative position at x ∈ Spec R. Define Gr_{≤μ} = {(E,β) ∈ Gr : Inv(β) ≤ μ}, a closed subspace by Lemma 1.22, and Gr_μ = {(E,β) ∈ Gr : Inv(β) = μ}, open in Gr_{≤μ}. Gr_{≤μ} is called the (spherical) Schubert variety and Gr_μ the Schubert cell. ϖ^μ ∈ Gr is the image of ϖ under μ.
items.note: The paper writes 'two G-torsors over O'; D_{F,K} is meant. Openness of Gr_μ holds because there are only finitely many dominant μ′ < μ. The GL_n version is B's G08; no item covers general G. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: n-fold convolution Grassmannian and bounded convolution maps
items.statement: Gr×̃⋯×̃Gr (n factors) classifies {(E_i, β_i)}_{i=1..n}, with E_i G-torsors on D_{F,R} and β_i: E_i|_{D*_{F,R}} ≃ E_{i−1}|_{D*_{F,R}} (E_0 trivial). Setting m_i = β_1⋯β_i gives (2.1.1): (m_1, …, m_n): Gr×̃⋯×̃Gr ≃ Gr^n. The convolution map is m = m_n. For dominant μ• = (μ_1, …, μ_n), Gr_{≤μ•} = Gr_{≤μ_1}×̃⋯×̃Gr_{≤μ_n} is the closed subspace where Inv(β_i) ≤ μ_i. With |μ•| = Σμ_i, m restricts to (2.1.2) m: Gr_{≤μ•} → Gr_{≤|μ•|}, (E•, β•) ↦ (E_n, β_1⋯β_n). Gr_{μ•} = Gr_{μ_1}×̃⋯×̃Gr_{μ_n}, and (2.1.3) Gr_{≤μ•} = ∪_{μ′•≤μ•} Gr_{μ′•} is a stratification (μ′• ≤ μ• meaning μ′_i ≤ μ_i for each i). The n-fold convolution is A1⋆⋯⋆An = m_!(A1⊠̃⋯⊠̃An), and IC_{μ•} := IC_{μ_1}⋆⋯⋆IC_{μ_n} = ⊕_λ V^λ_{μ•} ⊗ IC_λ with V^λ_{μ•} = Hom(IC_λ, IC_{μ•}).
items.note: S03 covers only the two-fold product. Proposition 2.3, Remark 2.4 and Corollaries 2.14–2.17 all use the n-fold version. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Semi-infinite orbits are locally closed and cover Gr (Iwasawa)
items.statement: Gr_U is represented by an inductive limit of perfect affine spaces. Since U\G is quasi-affine, Gr_U → Gr_G is a locally closed embedding (Proposition 1.20). S_λ := LU·ϖ^λ = ϖ^λ·Gr_U is locally closed in Gr_G, with S_0 = Gr_U. By the Iwasawa decomposition, Gr_G = ∪_{λ ∈ X_•} S_λ. Over S_λ the L^+G-torsor LG → Gr_G has the canonical L^+U-reduction LU → S_λ, n ↦ ϖ^λ n mod L^+G.
items.note: S04 only defines S_λ and CT_λ. Prop. 1.20 is stated for target GL_n. The application to U ⊂ G follows by applying it to U → GL_n (GL_n/U is quasi-affine since U has no characters) and using that Gr_G ⊂ Gr_{GL_n} is closed. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: The 2ρ^∨ torus action; attracting and repelling semi-infinite orbits
items.statement: Let 2ρ^∨ be the sum of the positive coroots (w.r.t. B), a cocharacter of G. The projection L_p^+G_m → G_m has a unique section (the Teichmüller torus), giving G_m^{p^{-∞}} → L^+G_m → L^+T ⊂ L^+G via L^+(2ρ^∨). The induced G_m^{p^{-∞}}-action on Gr_G has fixed points {ϖ^λ : λ ∈ X_•}, and S_λ is the attracting locus of ϖ^λ (s → 0). With B^- the opposite Borel and U^- its unipotent radical, the opposite semi-infinite orbits S_λ^- = LU^-·ϖ^λ are the repelling loci. S̄^-_λ = ∪_{λ′≥λ} S^-_{λ′} (Proposition 2.5).
items.note: This is the input for (2.2.10) and for Corollary 2.10. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: (Quasi-)minuscule coweights and the set M
items.statement: A dominant coweight μ is minuscule (resp. quasi-minuscule) if all weights (resp. all nonzero weights) of V_μ lie in a single W-orbit. For simple G, the quasi-minuscule non-minuscule coweight is the short dominant coroot θ; the paper denotes the corresponding root by θ^∨. Δ_θ is the set of simple coroots W-conjugate to θ, which for simple G are the short simple coroots. M is the set of minimal elements of X_•^+ \ {0}; the paper asserts that this is exactly the set of nonzero quasi-minuscule coweights, minuscule ones included.
items.note: The equality 'minimal elements = nonzero quasi-minuscule' is asserted without proof. It is standard: the minimal dominant element of a nontrivial coset of the coroot lattice is minuscule, and the minimal nonzero dominant elements of the coroot lattice are the θ of the simple factors. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Faithful representations with quasi-affine quotient ([PR08, §1.b])
items.statement: For a smooth affine group scheme G over a Dedekind domain there is a linear representation ρ: G → GL_n (a closed embedding) with GL_n/G quasi-affine.
items.note: Black box; with Proposition 1.20 it gives Theorem 1.4 over O_0. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Affine quotient for reductive group schemes ([Alp14, Cor. 9.7.7])
items.statement: If G is reductive over O, then ρ: G → GL_n can be chosen with GL_n/G affine.
items.note: Black box; with Proposition 1.20 it makes Gr_G → Gr_{GL_n} a closed embedding, giving ind-perfect properness for reductive G. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Kottwitz's characterization of X_•(T)_Γ ([Kot97, §2])
items.statement: A functor from F-tori to abelian groups satisfying the conditions of [Kot97, §2] is canonically isomorphic to T ↦ X_•(T)_{Gal(F̄/F)}. The paper applies this to T ↦ π_0(LT) to prove Proposition 1.21 for tori.
items.note: The exact list of conditions should be imported from Kot97 §2; the paper does not state them. The z-extension reduction is also used without detail. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Stratified semismall maps preserve perversity ([MV07, Lemma 4.3])
items.statement: If m: Gr_{≤μ•} → Gr is stratified semismall with respect to the stratification (2.1.3) and the L^+G-orbits (Proposition 2.3), then m_!(A_1⊠̃⋯⊠̃A_n) is perverse for A_i ∈ P_{L^+G}(Gr_{≤μ_i}).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.3, p. 432 (cited); used again in Corollary 2.15, p. 439
items.note: This is the direction 2.3 ⇒ 2.2; the converse is sketched in the paper. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Parity of the stalks of IC_μ
items.statement: For μ ∈ X_•^+ and λ ≤ μ, the cohomology sheaves H^i(IC_μ|_{Gr_λ}) vanish unless i ≡ ⟨2ρ,μ⟩ (mod 2), which is also ≡ ⟨2ρ,λ⟩ by Lemma 1.25.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1, p. 430 ([Lus83], [Gai01, Prop. 1]; Demazure resolution (1.4.2) with fibres paved by perfect affine spaces)
items.note: This is used for semisimplicity (Lemma 2.1). As in [MV07, Prop. 3.10], it is also needed to justify the isomorphism in the proof of Corollary 2.9: lower strata then contribute only in degrees ≤ (2ρ,λ) − 2. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Connected stabilizers; simple objects of P_{L^+G}(Gr_G)
items.statement: For μ ∈ X_•^+, the stabilizer L^+G ∩ ϖ^μL^+Gϖ^{-μ} of ϖ^μ is connected. Hence IC_μ|_{Gr_μ} = Q̄_ℓ[⟨2ρ,μ⟩], its restriction to each stratum Gr_λ is constant, and the irreducible objects of P_{L^+G}(Gr_G) are exactly the IC_μ, μ ∈ X_•^+.
items.note: Asserted without proof (standard). S02 records only the semisimplicity lemma. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Subcategory Sat^0_G of minimal convolutions
items.statement: Sat^0_G is the full additive subcategory of Sat_G spanned by objects isomorphic to IC_μ1 ⋆ ⋯ ⋆ IC_μm with μ• ⊂ M (M = minimal elements of X_•^+ ∖ {0}); it is a monoidal subcategory. Sat^{0,op}_G ⊂ Sat^op_G is defined in the same way.
items.note: Used in Lemma 2.16 and in the proof of Lemma 2.23 (monoidal structure of Id'). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Equivariant coefficient rings of parahorics
items.statement: (2.3.3) For (the p-adic jet group of) a parahoric P ⊇ T with reductive quotient L̄_P, let W_P ⊂ W̃ be its Weyl group and W̄_P the image in W̄. Then R_{L̄_P,ℓ} = R_{T̄,ℓ}^{W̄_P}; in particular R_{Ḡ,ℓ} = R_{T̄,ℓ}^{W̄} ⊂ R_{L̄_P,ℓ} ⊂ R_{T̄,ℓ} for every P.
items.note: Used in Lemma 2.19 (equality of the two R-structures) and in Lemma 2.32. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Ordinary cohomology as base change of equivariant cohomology
items.statement: For A ∈ Sat_G there is a canonical isomorphism H^*(A) = Q̄_ℓ ⊗_{R_{Ḡ,ℓ}} H^*_{L+G}(A), where R_{Ḡ,ℓ} → Q̄_ℓ is the augmentation ('by an easy spectral sequence argument').
items.note: Used for Proposition 2.20 and in Lemmas 2.27, 2.31 and 2.32 ('specializing along R → Q̄_ℓ'). Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of the commutativity constraint
items.statement: Proposition 2.21: for every A_1, A_2 ∈ Sat_G there is a unique isomorphism c_{A1,A2}: A_1⋆A_2 ≃ A_2⋆A_1 such that H^*(c_{A1,A2}), transported by the monoidal isomorphisms of Proposition 2.20, is the usual flip c_vect: H^*(A_1)⊗H^*(A_2) ≃ H^*(A_2)⊗H^*(A_1). Uniqueness holds because H^* is faithful; existence is proved in §§2.4.2–2.4.5.
items.note: The central statement of §2.4. O12 is its construction and O13 its corollary, but the proposition itself has no item. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Finite-level correspondence between Gr and Gr^op
items.statement: Let (LG)_≤μ be the preimage of Gr_≤μ in LG, and choose m with L^+G^(m) ⊂ L^+G ∩ ϖ^μL^+Gϖ^{−μ}. Then (2.4.1) is Gr_≤μ ←π_m Gr^(m)_≤μ = (LG)_≤μ/L^+G^(m) →φ_m L^+G\(LG)_≤μ = Gr^op_≤μ. Here π_m is an L^mG-torsor, so π_m^*[m dim G] preserves perversity, while φ_m is not known to be perfectly smooth (Remark 2.25(ii)). For μ• ⊂ M, the analogous diagram on p. 446 uses levels (m_1,…,m_n) such that L^+G acts on Gr^(m_i)_≤μi through L^{m_{i−1}}G.
items.note: The basis of Lemmas 2.23–2.24, Corollary 2.26 and Lemma 2.27. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Opposite resolution of Gr^op_≤μ
items.statement: For μ quasi-minuscule but not minuscule, Gr~^op_≤μ := Q_0\Q_0 ×^{Q_{1/4}} Q_{1/2} ×^{Q_{3/4}} Q_1 = Q_{1/4}\Q_{1/2} ×^{Q_{3/4}} Q_1, with π^op_μ: Gr~^op_≤μ → Gr^op_≤μ, (g,g') ↦ gg'ϖ^μ. Gr~^(m)_≤μ is defined so that both squares over (2.4.1) are Cartesian. Hence φ_m^*IC^op_μ ⊕ φ_m^*C^op ≃ φ_m^*(π^op_μ)_*Q̄_ℓ[d] ≃ (π^(m)_μ)_*Q̄_ℓ[d] ≃ π_m^*(π_μ)_*Q̄_ℓ[d] ≃ π_m^*IC_μ ⊕ π_m^*C, with d = (2ρ,μ).
items.note: Gives id'_μ for quasi-minuscule μ. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Normalized (equivariant) intersection cohomology
items.statement: IH_{L+G}(Gr_≤μ) := H^*_{L+G}(Gr, IC_μ[−(2ρ,μ)]) and IH^*(Gr_≤μ) := H^*(Gr, IC_μ[−(2ρ,μ)]), and similarly for Gr^op_≤μ; these are concentrated in degrees 0,…,2(2ρ,μ).
items.note: Lemmas 2.27 and 2.30 are stated in this normalization. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Automorphism Θ of H^*
items.statement: For A ∈ P_{L+G}(Gr), Θ: H^*(A) ≃δ H^*(θ^*A) ≃γ H^*(Id'∘θ^*A) ≃H^*(e) H^*(A). Lemmas 2.27–2.28 imply that, under the Künneth isomorphisms, H^*(c'_{A1,A2})∘Θ_{A1⋆A2} = (Θ⊗Θ)∘c_vect.
items.note: Lemma 2.29 computes Θ. For the argument to close, c_vect in this diagram must be the Koszul-signed flip (see the new issue). Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Open-orbit comparison Θ̊_μ
items.statement: θ restricts to an isomorphism of L^+G-orbits Gr^op_μ ≃ Gr_μ, and Θ̊_μ: H^*(Gr_μ) ≃θ^* H^*(Gr^op_μ) ≃γ H^*(Gr_μ), with γ built as in Lemma 2.27. Convention (p. 450): H(N_μ)δ is written θ^*.
items.note: Lemma 2.32 (item O08) is about this map. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Normalized IC complex C_μ and its stalks
items.statement: C_μ is IC_μ shifted so that C_μ|_{Gr_μ} = Q̄_ℓ in degree 0, i.e. C_μ = IC_μ[−(2ρ,μ)], as in [LY13, published §3.4]. The page prints IC_μ[(2ρ,μ)]; see E16. For λ ≤ μ, i_λ: Gr_λ → Gr_≤μ is the inclusion and H^j_λC_μ := H^j(i_λ^*C_μ), which is constant along Gr_λ and vanishes for odd j (Demazure resolution, (1.4.2)).
items.note: Needed for P_{d_λ,d_μ}(q) = Σ dim H^{2j}_λC_μ q^j and for Lemma 2.34. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Stalk involution H^j_λΨ_μ
items.statement: H^j_λΨ_μ: H^j_λC_μ = H^j_λθ^*C_μ ≃ H^j_λC^op_μ ≃ H^j_λC_μ, where the middle isomorphism is N_μ ((2.4.2)) and the last is Corollary 2.26. It is an involution ('Clearly').
items.note: Lemma 2.34 (item O09) computes it. The involution property is asserted only as 'clearly'; the argument is analogous to Lemma 2.31. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Stratification filtration on IH^*(Gr_≤μ)
items.statement: Extend ≤ on X_•^+ to a total order and put Gr_<λ = ⊔_{λ'<λ}Gr_{λ'}, with closed embeddings i_<λ and i_≤λ into Gr_≤μ. The sequences ⋯ → H^i(Gr_<λ, i^!_<λC_μ) → H^i(Gr_≤λ, i^!_≤λC_μ) → H^i(Gr_λ, i^!_λC_μ) → ⋯ split into short exact sequences, because all odd cohomology vanishes. They define the filtration Im(H^i(Gr_≤λ, i^!_≤λC_μ) → IH^*(Gr_≤μ)), whose graded pieces are ⊕_{λ≤μ} H^i(Gr_λ, i^!_λC_μ), and similarly on Gr^op_≤μ. θ^* and γ preserve the filtrations, and gr Θ = ⊕_λ Θ̊_λ ⊗ H^*_{λ,!}Ψ_μ, where H^*_{λ,!}Ψ_μ is the inverse of the dual of H^*_λΨ_μ.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.30 assuming Lemma 2.34, p. 452
items.note: The reduction of Lemma 2.30 to Lemmas 2.32 and 2.34. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: ω^* = ω^{−1} for length-zero elements (cited)
items.statement: [LY13, Lemma 6.2] (published Lemma 7.2(1)): every element of the coset A^♮∗ ⊂ Aut(W,S) is an involution, i.e. a^* = a^{−1} for a ∈ A^♮. Zhu uses the consequence ω^* = ω^{−1} for ω ∈ Ω, which makes w ↦ ωw^*ω^{−1} an involution of W_a.
items.note: A black box from another paper. LY13 state it for an irreducible affine Weyl group; in Zhu's Ω ≅ X_•/(coroot lattice) it also follows directly, since ∗ acts by −w_0 ≡ −1 modulo coroots. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Longest double-coset elements are ⋄-twisted involutions (cited)
items.statement: [Lus12, Prop. 8.2] (case ⋄ = ∗) and [LY13, Th. 6.3(1)] (published Th. 7.3(1)): each (W_J, W_J^⋄)-double coset in W_a is stable under w ↦ (w^⋄)^{−1}; in particular its longest element lies in I_⋄.
items.note: A black box; needed for P^{σ,⋄}_{d_λ,d_μ} to be defined. Missing: routed to route 18.

items.name: Monoidality of CT via T̄-equivariant cohomology (cited method)
items.statement: [Zhu16, Prop. 5.3.14]: in equal characteristic, the monoidal structure on the weight functor CT compatible with H^*∘CT ≃ H^* can be built purely locally from T̄-equivariant cohomology H^*_T̄ of the semi-infinite orbits. Zhu asserts the argument carries over because S_λ is stable under T̄^{p^{−∞}} ⊂ L^+T ⊂ L^+G.
items.note: The whole proof of Proposition 2.36 is this reference. Missing: routed to route 8.

items.name: Superbasic σ-conjugacy class
items.statement: A basic σ-conjugacy class in G(L) that does not meet any proper Levi subgroup of G defined over F is called superbasic.
items.note: Used in Proposition 3.3 and in the reduction of Theorem 3.1. For G_F = Res_{E/F} GL_n, b is superbasic iff J_b is anisotropic modulo the centre (rk_F J_b = 1). By Lemma 3.7(3) this passes to Nm b, which the last line of the proof of Proposition 3.3 uses implicitly. Missing: routed to route 15.

items.name: Dimension formula for superbasic GL_n ([Vie06], transferred to mixed characteristic)
items.statement: (Cited: [Vie06].) Let H = GL_n over O_E and let b ∈ GL_n(L) be superbasic (for σ_E). If X_≤μ(b) ≠ ∅, then dim X_≤μ(b) = ⟨ρ, μ − ν_b⟩ − ½ def(b) = ⟨ρ, μ − ν_b⟩ − (n − 1)/2. Viehmann proved this in equal characteristic. The paper asserts that 'the same arguments apply here' (p. 456) and that 'one can argue exactly the same as [Vie06] to complete the proof' (p. 460).
items.locator: p. 456 (after Theorem 3.1); end of the proof of Proposition 3.3, p. 460
items.note: This is the only case of Theorem 3.1 not reduced to something else in the paper. It is a black box, and the mixed-characteristic transfer is only asserted. def(b) = n − 1 because J_b is D^× for a central division algebra D over E of dimension n^2, whose split rank is 1. The paper states the PGL_n form on p. 456 and the GL_n form on p. 460. Missing: routed to route 15.

items.name: Rapoport–Zink functor of quasi-isogenies M_{X_0}
items.statement: (k = F̄_p, W = W(k); Nilp_W is the category of W-algebras in which p is nilpotent.) For a p-divisible group X_0 over k, M_{X_0} assigns to R ∈ Nilp_W the groupoid of pairs (X, ι), where X is a p-divisible group over Spec R and ι : X_0 ⊗_k R/p → X ⊗_R R/p is a quasi-isogeny.
items.note: Target of Theorem 3.10(1),(2) and of Proposition 3.11 (GL_h case). Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: Representability of M_{X_0} ([RZ96])
items.statement: (Cited: Rapoport–Zink [RZ96].) M_{X_0} is represented by a separated formal scheme over W, formally smooth and formally locally of finite type over W.
items.note: Black box. It makes M̄ (the special fibre) and its perfection meaningful in Proposition 3.11. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: Crystalline Tate tensor of a p-divisible group (after [Kim13])
items.statement: Let R ∈ Nilp_W and let X be a p-divisible group over Spec R. Let 1 := D(Q_p/Z_p) be the filtered F-crystal with 1_{R'} = R' for every PD thickening R' → R, F(1) = 1 and Fil^1 1_R = 0. A (crystalline) Tate tensor of X is a morphism of crystals t : 1 → D(X)^⊗ such that t_R : 1_R → D(X)_R^⊗ is compatible with the filtrations and the induced map t : 1 → D(X)^⊗[1/p] of isocrystals is Frobenius-invariant.
items.note: Used in Definition 3.8(2),(3). D(X)^⊗ contains duals, so its Frobenius is defined only after inverting p. That is why invariance is imposed on D(X)^⊗[1/p]. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: The tensors s_i as Tate tensors of the framing X_0
items.statement: Via ε, regard s_i ∈ Λ^⊗ as elements of D(X_0)^⊗. G fixes the s_i, and they are defined over Z_p, so bσ fixes them and they are F-invariant in D(X_0)^⊗[1/p]. The cocharacter ρμ fixes the s_i, so they lie in Fil^0(D(X_0)^⊗_{F̄_p}). Hence s_i : 1 → D(X_0)^⊗, 1 ↦ s_i, are Tate tensors of X_0.
items.note: Used in Definition 3.8(3) ('sends t_i to s_i ⊗ 1'). The Fil^0 step uses (2) of the framing. It also holds whenever the Hodge filtration is split by any G-valued cocharacter; see E21. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: Cartesian square for the convolution map on iterated ADLVs, and fibre bound
items.statement: Let H be over O_E, b' ∈ H(L), μ• = (μ_1, …, μ_d) dominant, |μ•| = Σ μ_i, and let m : Gr_≤μ• → Gr_≤|μ•| be the convolution map (§2.2). By (3.1.4) and (3.1.5), X^H_≤μ•(b'σ_E) → X^H_≤|μ•|(b'σ_E) is the base change of 1 ×̃ m : Gr_H ×̃ Gr_≤μ• → Gr_H ×̃ Gr_≤|μ•|. Hence its fibre over a point whose endpoint g^{-1} b' σ_E(g) lies in Gr_λ is isomorphic to m^{-1}(ϖ^λ) ∩ Gr_≤μ•. By the proof of Proposition 2.3, this fibre has dimension ≤ (ρ_H, |μ•| − λ).
items.note: The fibre bound in the proof of Proposition 2.3 is for Gr_μ• ∩ m^{-1}(ϖ^λ). For Gr_≤μ• it follows from the pieces Gr_μ'• with μ'• ≤ μ•, since (ρ, |μ'•|) ≤ (ρ, |μ•|). This is the input of D11 and of E20. Missing: routed to route 15.

items.name: Norm map on σ-conjugacy classes (Remark 3.6)
items.statement: b ↦ Nm b induces a map from σ-conjugacy classes in G(L) to σ_E-conjugacy classes in H(L) (E embedded in L via τ_0). Indeed, Nm(g^{-1} b σ(g)) = g_{τ_0}^{-1} (Nm b) σ_E(g_{τ_0}) (with τ_i = σ^{-i}τ_0).
items.note: Stated without proof. It is not used later, except implicitly when the Res_{E/F} GL_n case is reduced to GL_n with Nm b superbasic. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Schematic and fpqc maps of k-spaces
items.statement: A map f : F -> G in Sp_k is schematic if F x_G T is a scheme for every scheme T. A representable map is fpqc if in addition F x_G T is faithfully flat over T for every affine T and some quasi-compact open subset of F x_G T maps surjectively onto T.
items.note: A02 covers algebraic spaces and representability but not fpqc maps. These are needed for (A.1.2), the definition of torsors (A.1.3) and Lemma A.7(10). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Frobenius and perfection are universal homeomorphisms; scheme criterion
items.statement: For an algebraic space X over k, sigma_X is a universal homeomorphism (from the scheme case by Lemma A.2). Hence eps : X^{p^-inf} -> X is a universal homeomorphism, and X is a scheme if and only if X^{p^-inf} is a scheme.
items.note: A08 records only the universal-homeomorphism part. The scheme criterion is asserted with a pointer to Lemma A.7. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Perfection equivalence preserves scheme objects
items.statement: The equivalence X_et = X^{p^-inf}_et of Proposition A.5 preserves the subcategories of scheme objects in X_et and X^{p^-inf}_et.
items.note: Follows from Remark A.4. Used in the proof of Proposition A.15 (an étale map of perfect schemes descends to an étale map of schemes V'_i -> U'). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Quotient stack [X/H] and free quotient X/H
items.statement: For a k-space X with an action of an affine group scheme H, [X/H] is the fpqc quotient stack whose R-points form the groupoid of pairs (E, phi), with E an H-torsor on Spec R and phi : E -> X an H-equivariant morphism. If the action is free, [X/H] is a k-space and X -> [X/H] is an H-torsor, written X/H.
items.note: Printed with 'phi : E -> Y' (see E23). This is the quotient in Theorem A.29 and Lemma A.11. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Torsors and quotients in Sp^pf_k
items.statement: For a perfect affine group scheme H, H^pf is in Sp^pf_k. For a perfect space X with an H^pf-action, [X/H^pf] is the analogous stack on Aff^pf_k; if the action is free, [X/H^pf] is a perfect space, X -> [X/H^pf] is an H^pf-torsor, and one writes X/H^pf. If X is a perfect algebraic space, then by Lemma A.12 an action of H^pf on X^pf is the same as an action of H on X, and if it is free, X^pf/H^pf = (X/H)^pf. From here on a perfect algebraic space and its image in Sp^pf_k are both written X; a general space F has image F^pf.
items.note: Every quotient in the main text (e.g. Gr = LG/L+G) is taken in this sense. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Representability and properties of maps of perfect spaces
items.statement: By Lemma A.12 it makes sense to ask whether a presheaf F on Aff^pf_k is represented by a perfect algebraic space, and whether a map F -> G of presheaves is representable by perfect algebraic spaces. Any property (P) of morphisms of algebraic spaces that is stable under base change and étale local on source and target then makes sense for representable morphisms of perfect spaces (e.g. open/closed immersions, étale morphisms, fpqc maps in Sp^pf_k).
items.note: Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Generic points of a qcqs algebraic space (cited)
items.statement: [St, Tag 03JG]: a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space S has an open dense subspace U that is a scheme. The generic points of |S| lie in |U| and are the generic points of U, so the residue field k(eta) at a generic point is defined.
items.note: Cited black box used to state Proposition A.15. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Weakly normal scheme/algebraic space
items.statement: A reduced scheme X of finite type over k is weakly normal if every finite birational universal homeomorphism f : Y -> X is an isomorphism. By [Man80] weak normality is local in the étale (even fppf) topology, so the notion makes sense for algebraic spaces of finite presentation over k.
items.note: The étale locality is a cited black box [Man80]. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: p-closed rings are weakly normal (cited, Yanagihara)
items.statement: A ring A (reduced, of characteristic p, as in the proof) is p-closed, meaning that every a in its total quotient ring with a^p in A lies in A, if and only if A is weakly normal ([Ito83], remark after Proposition 1, proved by Yanagihara).
items.note: Cited black box giving weak normality of the model X' built by (A.2.1). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Universal property (A.2.2) of the weakly normal model
items.statement: In the scheme case of Proposition A.15, X' = (|X|, O_{X'}) with O_{X'} = {f in O_X : f(eta_i) in K_i} is the pushout of the diagram of Spec K_i <- eta_i -> X (disjoint unions) in locally ringed spaces. Hence for every scheme Y the natural map Hom(X', Y) -> Hom(X, Y) x_{Hom(disjoint eta_i, Y)} Hom(disjoint Spec K_i, Y) is a bijection.
items.note: Used in the algebraic-space case of A.15, in Corollary A.16 and in Appendix B (p. 486, 'by (A.2.2)'). A21 records only existence and uniqueness of the model. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Perfect variety and perfect group variety
items.statement: Following [Ser60], a separated perfect k-scheme perfectly of finite type is called a perfect variety (Remark A.14), and a perfect group variety is a group object in the category of perfect varieties (A.2.2).
items.note: Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Serre: perfect groups come from finite-type groups (cited)
items.statement: [Ser60, Section 1.4, Prop. 10]: a pfp perfect group scheme H over k is the perfection of a group scheme H' of finite type over k.
items.note: Cited black box; Lemma A.26 then passes to H'_red. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Morphisms from limits into finitely presented targets (cited)
items.statement: ([Gro66, Section 8.14]; [CLO12, Prop. A.3.1]; [St, Tag 049I]) If Y' is locally of finite presentation over k and X = lim_i X_i is the limit of an inverse system of qcqs algebraic spaces with affine transition maps, then Hom_k(X, Y') = colim_i Hom_k(X_i, Y'). Applied to X = lim_sigma X', this factors eps f : X -> Y' through some X'^{(m)} (Prop. A.17) and factors the cocycles f_ij and the relations h_ijk at a finite level (Lemma A.22).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.17, pp. 472-473; proof of Lemma A.22, p. 474
items.note: Cited black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Frobenius-twisted k-structure X'^{(m)}
items.statement: For an algebraic space X' over k and m >= 0, X'^{(m)} denotes X' with the k-structure X' --sigma^m--> X' -> Spec k. If X' is a model of X, so is X'^{(m)}.
items.note: Used in Lemma A.22 and Appendix B (p. 484). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Perfections of valuation rings
items.statement: The perfection of a valuation ring is a valuation ring, and every perfect local ring contained in a perfect field K is dominated by a perfect valuation ring of K.
items.locator: Proposition A.20 and its proof, p. 473
items.note: Inputs to the perfect valuative criterion. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Perfect Grassmannians and projective spaces
items.statement: Gr^{p^-inf}(i, n) := Gr^{p^-inf}(i, E) for X = Spec k and E = k^n; P^{p^-inf}(E) := Gr^{p^-inf}(1, E); P^{n,p^-inf} := Gr^{p^-inf}(1, n+1). O(1) on P^{n,p^-inf} is the tautological rank-one quotient O^{n+1} -> O(1).
items.locator: After Corollary A.23 and Remark A.24, p. 474
items.note: Used in A.3.2 (Chern classes) and in section 1.2 (p. 422). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Étale-local finite flat presentations of stacks with quasi-finite diagonal (cited)
items.statement: ([KM97, Lemma 3.3, Prop. 4.2]; [Con, Lemmas 2.1, 2.2]) An Artin stack X' of finite presentation over k with quasi-finite diagonal admits an étale cover Y' -> X' by an Artin stack Y' that is separated and of finite presentation over k, together with a finite flat cover Z' -> Y' by a quasi-projective k-scheme Z'.
items.note: Cited black box, applied to [X'/H'], whose diagonal H' x X' -> X' x X' is affine and quasi-finite. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Invariant affine neighbourhoods and quotients by finite locally free groupoids (cited)
items.statement: ([St, Tag 03JE]) If (U, R, s, t, c) is a groupoid scheme with s, t finite locally free and t(s^{-1}(u)) lies in an affine open, then u has an R-invariant affine open neighbourhood. ([St, Tag 03BL]) If U = Spec A and R = Spec B are affine with s, t finite locally free and C is the equalizer of s, t : A => B, then |U| -> |Spec C| is surjective, two points have the same image iff some r in R joins them, and (Spec C)(k) = U(k)/R(k) for k algebraically closed.
items.note: Cited black boxes: the reduction to affine U', V' and the surjectivity of V -> U x_X U. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Splitting a finite algebra and the image of Spec (cited)
items.statement: ([St, Tag 0531]) For a finite ring map R -> S there is a finite free extension R subset R'' such that S tensor_R R'' is a quotient of R''[T_1..T_n]/(P_1(T_1),...,P_n(T_n)) with P_i(T) = prod_{j=1..d_i}(T - a_ij), a_ij in R''. ([St, Tag 0532]) If S = R[T_1..T_n]/J with J containing such split P_i(T_i), and J_k is the image of J under T_i -> a_{i k_i}, then the image of Spec S -> Spec R is V(intersection_k J_k).
items.note: Cited black boxes. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Flatness modulo ideals with zero intersection (cited)
items.statement: ([St, Tag 0522]) If M/I_1M is flat over R/I_1 and M/I_2M is flat over R/I_2, then M/(I_1 cap I_2)M is flat over R/(I_1 cap I_2). By induction, if M/I_kM is flat over R/I_k for finitely many ideals with intersection 0, then M is flat over R.
items.note: Cited black box. In the perfect setting the intersection of the perfected J_k is exactly 0, so the Noetherian hypothesis of Stacks Tag 0533 (Ferrand) is not needed. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Zariski's main theorem for algebraic spaces (cited)
items.statement: ([St, Tag 05W7]) A quasi-finite separated morphism of algebraic spaces X -> Y with Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated factors as a quasi-compact open immersion followed by a finite morphism.
items.note: Cited black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Six operations, perverse sheaves and IC on perfect spaces
items.statement: For separated pfp perfect algebraic spaces, the six operations on D^b_c(-, Qlbar) are defined through models (Proposition A.17). Proper base change holds for perfectly proper maps and smooth base change for perfectly smooth maps. Perverse sheaves P(X), the Goresky-MacPherson intermediate extension and IC_X are defined as usual. The paper adds that IC_X restricted to a perfectly smooth open U is canonically Qlbar[2 dim X](dim X), a slip for Qlbar[dim X] (E25).
items.note: E01 records only D^b_c. This item is the setting of every perverse sheaf in the main text. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Characteristic classes of G-torsors (A.3.2)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over k and R_{G,l} = Sym(g*_{Qlbar}(-1))^{G_{Qlbar}}. For a G-torsor E on a separated pfp perfect X (equivalently a G^{p^-inf}-torsor), c(E) : R_{G,l} -> H^*(X_kbar, Qlbar) is built as follows. For a Borel B of G_kbar with unipotent radical U, T = B/U and Weyl group W, the T-torsor E_kbar/U -> E_kbar/B gives c(E_kbar/U) : R_{T,l} -> H^*(E_kbar/B, Qlbar) via Chern classes, and R_{G,l} = R_{T,l}^W maps into H^*(X_kbar, Qlbar), a subring of H^*(E_kbar/B, Qlbar). For a general connected G, c(E) := c(E^red) for the induced torsor under the reductive quotient G^red. Remark A.33: equivalently c(E) = c(E') for a model E' -> X' (Lemma A.22), independent of the model.
items.note: E14 covers Chern classes of vector bundles and E13 the ring R. This construction for general torsors has no item. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Equivariant perverse sheaves for affine pfp groups
items.statement: Let J be an affine pfp perfect group scheme over k (perfectly smooth by Lemma A.26) acting on a separated pfp perfect algebraic space X. P_J(X) is the category of perverse sheaves on X together with an isomorphism between the pullbacks along the two maps J x X => X (action, projection), satisfying the usual compatibility conditions.
items.note: Base definition that (A.3.3), (A.3.4) and E10 refine. Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Equivariant cohomology via finite-dimensional approximations
items.statement: For A in P_J(X) (or a J-equivariant complex) and J_0 a smooth model of J (Lemma A.26), choose J_0-torsors E_n -> B_n with closed embeddings B_n in B_{n+1} and H^*(colim B_n) = H^*(BJ_0). For example, embed J_0 in GL_r with GL_r/J_0 quasi-affine, let E_n = S_{n,r} be the Stiefel variety over Gr(r, n) and B_n = E_n/J_0, a scheme. Qlbar [x] A on E_n^{p^-inf} x X descends by (A.3.3) to Qlbar [x]~ A on the twisted product E_n x~ X, a separated pfp perfect algebraic space by A.1.3. Set H^*_J(X_kbar, A) := H^*(colim_n (E_n^{p^-inf} x~ X)_kbar, Qlbar [x]~ A). This is a module over H^*(BJ_0), which equals R_{G,l} for connected J_0 with reductive quotient G = J_0^red.
items.note: E13 records only the identification of H^*(BJ_0). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Equivariant cohomology of a free quotient (A.3.5)
items.statement: If J_1 in J acts freely on X with quotient X-bar = [X/J_1] and q : X -> X-bar, then H^*_J(X_kbar, q^*A) = H^*_{J/J_1}(X-bar_kbar, A).
items.note: Used on p. 441 ('by (A.3.5)') to define the R_{Gbar,l}-bimodule structure on H^*_{L+G}(A). E11 covers only (A.3.3). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Remark B.5: mixed versus equal characteristic Schubert varieties
items.statement: Gr'_{≤μ} is probably not isomorphic to its equal characteristic counterpart Gr^♭_{≤μ} for general μ (cf. Remark 1.15). By the geometric Satake equivalence their intersection cohomology is isomorphic; the paper adds, without proof, 'or more generally, their motives'.
items.note: The IC comparison follows from geometric Satake in both settings (IH^*(Gr_{≤μ}) ≅ V_μ). The motivic claim is not proved (new source issue). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Conjecture I plus point separation implies Conjecture II
items.statement: Assume Conjecture I. If Γ(\overline{Gr}_N, L_det) separates points (for all distinct x, y ∈ \overline{Gr}_N there is s with s(x) = 0 and s(y) ≠ 0), then Conjecture II holds.
items.note: Stated without proof. Plausible for perfect schemes: tangent directions carry no information, and a proper universally injective map of perfect schemes onto its image is an isomorphism (Cor. A.16). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Canonical model \widetilde{Gr}'_N of the Demazure resolution
items.statement: Gr_N ⊂ \widetilde{Gr}_N is open dense (Lemma 1.18). Prop. A.15, applied with the function field of the canonical model Gr'_N = Gr'_{Nω_1}, gives a canonical weakly normal model \widetilde{Gr}'_N of \widetilde{Gr}_N.
items.note: This is the object in Prop. B.8. Only B13 mentions it. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Signature and degree force ker φ_i ⊂ X_{i−1}[p]
items.statement: For a chain in M_{N,h}, conditions (1) (signatures) and (2) (deg φ_i = p^{2i−1}) imply ker φ_i ⊂ X_{i−1}[p].
items.note: Checked: with covariant Dieudonné modules, the colengths ℓ_j of M(X_{i−1})_j ⊂ M(X_i)_j satisfy ℓ_j − ℓ_{j+1} = (change in Lie rank at τ_j). The signature change is +1 at j = i−1 and −1 at j = 2h−i, so ℓ_j = c+1 on the 2i−1 indices −(i−1),…,i−1 and c elsewhere. The degree gives 2hc + 2i − 1 = 2i − 1, so c = 0 and every ℓ_j ≤ 1. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: Conditions (3)–(4) cut out an irreducible component
items.statement: The moduli problem given by conditions (1)–(2) alone is a scheme closely related to Rapoport–Zink spaces. It is not irreducible in general, not even equidimensional, and conditions (3)–(4) cut out M_{N,h} inside it as an irreducible component.
items.note: Asserted without proof or example. For N ≤ 2 I checked that (3)–(4) determine all components of the step except the τ_0 line, which is consistent with Lemma B.7. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: M_{N,h}^{p^{−∞}} ≃ \widetilde{Gr}_N via the τ_0-Dieudonné chain
items.statement: Choose a trivialization D(X_0)_{τ_0} ≅ W(k)^n = E_0. Then (X_0 → ⋯ → X_N) ↦ (D(X_N)_{τ_0} → ⋯ → D(X_0)_{τ_0}) defines an isomorphism M_{N,h}^{p^{−∞}} ≃ \widetilde{Gr}_N (argument as in Prop. 3.11).
items.note: Used in Prop. B.8 and Lemma B.9. Sketch only; uses Dieudonné theory over perfect rings as in Prop. 3.11. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: The open locus \mathring{M}_{N,h} ≃ Gr'_N
items.statement: The chains for which ker(φ_N⋯φ_1: X_0 → X_N) is not contained in X_0[p^{N−1}] form an open subscheme \mathring{M}_{N,h} ⊂ M_{N,h}. It is isomorphic to Gr'_N = Gr'_{Nω_1}, compatibly with \widetilde{Gr}_N ≃ M_{N,h}^{p^{−∞}}.
items.note: Stated with 'one can show'. Consistency check: only the τ_0 component of the composite kernel has length N; the others have length < N. So the condition says that the τ_0 chain has type Nω_1, i.e. it lies over Gr_N. Missing: routed to route 17.

items.name: Equations for V_{2,3}
items.statement: V_{2,3}(R) = {(X, λ) ∈ M_2(W_3(R)) × R^× : [λ] det X = p²}. Write X = (a b; c d) with a = [a_0] + p[a_1] + p²[a_2], and similarly for b, c, d. Then det X ∈ p²W_3(R) iff a_0d_0 = b_0c_0 and (a_1 b_1; c_1 d_1)(d_0 −b_0; −c_0 a_0) + (a_0 b_0; c_0 d_0)(d_1 −b_1; −c_1 a_1) = 0 (B.3.1). Hence V_{2,3} is (the perfection of) an open subscheme of the affine scheme cut out by (B.3.1).
items.note: Checked: the matrix equation in (B.3.1) equals D·I, where D = a_0d_1 + a_1d_0 − b_0c_1 − b_1c_0 is the p-coefficient of det X. The Teichmüller carries vanish exactly because p > 2. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The functor W ⊂ V_{2,3} and the open locus W̃
items.statement: For perfect k-algebras R, W(R) is the set of X ∈ V_{2,3}(R) admitting X = Ag with g ∈ G(R) = GL_2(W_3(R)) and A = [[p+[x], −[y]], [[z], p−[x]]] ∈ M_2(W_3(R)), det A = p². W̃ ⊂ V_{2,3} is the open subscheme where a_1d_1 − b_1c_1 ∈ R^×.
items.note: Needed for the statement of Lemma B.11 (see the B18 fix). Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Decomposition claim on W̃
items.statement: Every X ∈ W̃(R) admits a decomposition X = Ag as in the definition of W, and A is unique. Explicitly, (x,y,z) is the unique solution of (B.3.2): (d_0 −b_0; −c_0 a_0)(x −y; z −x) = 0 and (d_1 −b_1; −c_1 a_1)(x −y; z −x) = −(d_0 −b_0; −c_0 a_0). It is given by (B.3.3): (x −y; z −x) = (b_1c_1 − a_1d_1)^{−1}(a_1 b_1; c_1 d_1)(d_0 −b_0; −c_0 a_0). Also g = (Ã^{−1}X̃ mod p³).
items.note: Checked: (B.3.2) is X^*A ≡ 0 mod p². The right side of (B.3.3) is traceless and has determinant det X_0/det X_1 = 0 (so x² = yz), and it satisfies the first equation of (B.3.2), all by (B.3.1). For the misprints in the printed proof, see E32 and E33. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: The action map U^{p^{−∞}} × L^3GL_2 → V is an isomorphism
items.statement: Lift U^{p^{−∞}} → \overline{Gr}_2 to U^{p^{−∞}} → \overline{Gr}_{2,3}, A ↦ (E_0, A, id), and let V ⊂ \overline{Gr}_{2,3} be the preimage of W under \overline{Gr}_{2,3} → V_{2,3}. Then the action map U^{p^{−∞}} × L^3GL_2 → V, (A, g) ↦ (E_0, A, g), is an isomorphism. It is a monomorphism by the uniqueness of A, and surjective on R-points by the definition of W and the argument of Lemma 1.10.
items.note: This is the actual content of the proof of Lemma B.10. It suffices because \overline{Gr}_{2,3} → \overline{Gr}_2 is an L^3GL_2-torsor (§1.2.2, h = 3 > N = 2). Missing: routed to route 6.

routes.title: Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: dominant subtraction and Demazure reduction
routes.reason: Reuse the existing candidate identifier and shared supplier; this is an additional source, not a second roadmap.
routes.brief: Import root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems), the existing weight-lattice interfaces from representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight), and local relative/affine root adapters from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1/RG2.4. Do not re-plan any upstream layer; reconcile their conflicting prose about lattice ownership by using the existing pinned root-datum carrier. Construct only the missing parabolic-representative/support adapters and Demazure product, with maximum characterization, simple recursion, associativity, monotonicity, support union and ordinary-product comparison. Prove the HN14 reduction-to-minimal-length theorem for affine twisted conjugacy. For an explicit full coweight lattice prove nonemptiness, lower-directedness and leastness of the dominant subtraction feasible set; export Prop.5.1, Cor.5.3 and the exact identity (λ−domλ1)−domλ2=λ−dom(λ1+λ2). Supply ρ∨_J and η∨_J on this full lattice, the root-sign/length lemmas used in (5.1)–(5.4), the minuscule exception and the 2ρ∨ bound. Do not identify the full lattice with the cocharacters of every G; G1 must be settled by an explicit comparison. Test A1 parity in P∨/Q∨, singular A2 representatives, s*s=s, diagram automorphisms, non-simply-laced dual root data and strict versus weak dominance. Every definition needs APIs and genuine unit examples. Suggested future Lean home: TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Demazure.lean and TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/DominantSubtraction.lean; no Lean implementation is supplied in this paper job. Follow-up: add finite and parabolic twisted Coxeter elements, their ellipticity and HY12's finite-Coxeter-part reduction theorem, preserving P∨ versus actual cocharacters and τ-saturated support. The shared generic Hecke/cocenter carrier belongs to SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, not a second algebra here. Consolidate the overlapping RootSystemsDominancePartII candidate from PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 into this already reused identifier, as also requested by PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26; retain their stable item ids and separate Stembridge/Frobenius-orbit obligations. The ²A2 regression /127 is mandatory: normalized subtraction and γ live in P∨ and cannot always be lifted to the original lattice. No such lift is a target. Additional Zhu17 scope: Add only the extended-affine/length-zero opposition adapters and longest finite-parabolic double-coset indexing used by Zhu2.35. Ordinary Coxeter/Bruhat theory stays upstream. The generic Hecke algebra and twisted KL module belong to SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters. Test A1, non-simply-laced root/coroot conversion, ω*=ω⁻¹ and exclusion of arbitrary double-coset elements.

Import Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1) for actual convolution algebras and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4 for Iwahori–Weyl data; import RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure for Demazure multiplication, RedMin and HY12 finite-Coxeter reduction. Add an early equal-parameter generic affine-Hecke algebra over Z[v,v^-1], its basis, Ω action and diagram automorphisms. Prove the twisted cocenter basis theorem, nonnegative class-polynomial recursion and positive product coefficients. A cocenter is a module quotient, not the center and not generally an algebra quotient. Prove He14 Proposition11.6 with full δ-support, μ≠0 and the corrected outside-parabolic descent, and derive a nonzero coefficient in a basic class for a t^γ with γ≠0 dominant and full δ-support, without a shrunken condition. HN14's based-ring/trace independence proof and twisted-component passage must be decomposed, not postulated. The ADLV roadmap owns dimension=degree and all geometry/characteristic transfer. Test rank-one quadratic normalization, all A2 products/associativity, diagram-twisted support and zero μ as a rejected input. Share the generic Iwahori presentation with the existing Bernstein-center lane through explicit specialization; do not make later Shimura trace formulas a prerequisite. Suggested future Lean modules: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Hecke/{GenericAffine,TwistedCocenter,ClassPolynomial}.lean. No Lean implementation is supplied here. Additional Zhu17 scope: Extend the already shared equal-parameter generic Hecke algebra by ordinary and Lusztig–Vogan twisted KL bases/modules. Prove Lusztig–Kato in the exact classical Satake normalization and the restricted identity P^(σ,⋄)_(x,y)(q)=P_(x,y)(−q) for the longest double-coset elements of Zhu2.35, using LY13 published7.3(2)/7.4 and independent equal-characteristic geometric Satake (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1). Import RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure for indexing. Never use mixed Satake to prove this numerical input. Distinguish the twisted module, cocenter and center; test A1 normalization and reject unrestricted polynomial identities.

routes.brief: Import Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas, HS0/HS2), geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve (GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:loop-geometry/GS0:Witt-geometry), Bun_G and Newton strata (BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0/BG1), ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1–RG2.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 and the proposed RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. Keep classical equal-characteristic ADLV schemes and mixed-characteristic perfect ADLV spaces separate from local shtuka diamonds; an actual comparison is needed where used. Construct X_w(b), η_σ, virtual dimension, reduction relations, generic Newton classes, cordiality, double-flat coweights and Levi alcoves. Cover split parts of Theorems2.1/3.1/3.2, Proposition3.3, MV cordial saturation with a known nonempty lower endpoint, and Theorem4.2: x t^λ is cordial with [b_xtλ]=[t^λ]. Prove the precise two-correspondence Theorem5.5, retaining every lattice, finite-type and perfection hypothesis. Final targets: for simple quasi-split G, shrunken w, λ_w^♦−ν_b strictly positive on every simple coroot and (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b, X_w(b) is nonempty exactly when κ(b)=κ(w) and supp_σ(η_σ(w))=S, and then dim=(ℓw+ℓη_σ(w)−def_G(b))/2−〈ν_b,ρ〉. Also prove Cor.6.4 with λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨ and the separate shrunken hypothesis. Gate execution on G1–G3: auxiliary/adjoint lattice realization, bounded/perfect fiber-dimension comparison, and the /120–122 basic-seed proof and transport (the explicit A2 example shows it need not be shrunken). Preserve the tame/good-characteristic restrictions of cited inputs until broader transport is proved. Use the corrected (J,x,σ) in §6.2, all overbars in §4.3, and the GHN erratum. Add basic/minuscule/wall/σ-twisted/rank-one and nonbasic-Levi tests; never infer all classes below the maximal Newton point from saturation alone. Suggested future Lean home: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineDeligneLusztig/{Basic,Reduction,Cordial,Dimension}.lean. This checkpoint is a design brief, not a verified proof closure or a Lean implementation. Follow-up: for γ≠0 use He14 Proposition11.6 with J=S, Proposition11.7 and its class-polynomial nonemptiness criterion, not its shrunken Theorem11.4. For γ=0 use the finite reductive quotient and Lang. Import generic cocenters/class polynomials from SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters and finite-Coxeter reduction from RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. The corrected twisted induction, HN cocenter proof, general datum/characteristic transfer and finite-parahoric Lang comparison remain explicit gates. G2 is now a local finite-type argument /123–126, not an assumption that the full ADLV has finitely many components. State Theorem5.5 in the working adjoint/full-coweight carrier. Theorem6.1 for the original group needs a proved componentwise descent, not integral lifting of γ. Use /130–134 for the fibre-dimension and compatible-perfection inputs; the explicit cartesian squares are /125. Additional Zhu17 scope: Add Zhu’s unramified affine-Grassmannian dimension theorem for NONEMPTY X_≤μ(b): dim=⟨ρ,μ−ν_b⟩−def_G(b)/2. Import BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0/BG1 and GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0/GS2 for perfect geometry and convolution semismallness. Split basic-Levi, superbasic, adjoint and Res GL_n reductions; construct ordered Frobenius norms and iterated ADLVs. Apply fibre estimates on exact endpoint strata and justify top-stratum nonemptiness/full dimension separately. Read GHKR, Hamacher, CKV and Viehmann original proof inputs. Tests include torus Kottwitz mismatch, d=1 norm, noncommuting d=2 norm and defect rank conventions. Corrections the design must carry: Theorems 0.5 and 3.1 need X_μ(b) nonempty (E19); the proof of Proposition 3.3 should use the exact stratum X_λ (E20); and in §3.2 the element b must lie in G(W)σ(μ)(p)G(W), as in Howard–Pappas, for the Hodge filtration of type μ, otherwise Theorem 3.10(3) fails when {μ} is not defined over Q_p (E64); the dimension results are unaffected.

routes.brief: Reuse the KPZ26 integral continuation after Hecke stacks and local shtukas (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas). Import Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0/SF.1), Witt flag geometry (GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:Witt-geometry), local reductive groups (ReductiveGroupsPartII), and isocrystals (BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0/BG1). Construct perfect local Hecke and shtuka stacks, their height bounds, reductive and higher restricted quotients, and the actual Iwahori truncation correspondence. Prove van Hoften2.3.4 Cartesian as a two-fiber square via equal-band gerbes,2.3.9 weak smoothness with the extra kernel gerbe, and2.4.6 Newton quotient [underline J_b(Qp)\X] on the pro-etale site. Keep the locally profinite topology; do not replace it by a discrete constant group. Prove the canonical special-fiber comparison with PR/DvHKZ, then compare Hoff and SYZ normalizations using explicit Frobenius and frame-change formulas. The crystalline global local-model diagram is a consumer of the tensor-display and tangent compatibility theorem, never its proof. Tests cover nontrivial stabilizers, zero-rank torus, cofinal truncations, the omitted kernel gerbe, and noncommutative sigma-conjugacy transport. Additional Zhu17 scope: Add the unramified Hodge-type RZ representability and canonical perfected-special-fibre ADLV comparison of Zhu3.10–3.12, importing the finite-flat tensor supplier and the shared ADLV dimension owner. For p>2 and nonempty moduli, deduce the dimension formula without a ramified extension. Add the OE-linear chain moduli M_(N,h) over F̄_p with all four conditions, projective bundle tower for0≤i<h, canonical resolution-model comparison using D(X0)_τ0, and exact Hodge determinant exponents −p^i. routes.title: Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: the rational Gelfand symmetry proof
routes.reason: GS3:fusion explicitly retains the FS fusion proof. Zhu’s finite-level opposite-quotient, equivariant-bimodule and twisted-KL proof is a distinct substantial argument, while the category, convolution, weight and reconstruction outputs remain shared with GS2/GS4.
imports: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Witt-geometry and the early rational GS1/GS2 interfaces only
routes.brief: Extend Geometric Satake and fusion (GeometricSatakeAndFusion) with Zhu17’s rational one-leg alternative proof, not a second category or dual-group owner. Import common Witt geometry GS0, the early rational perverse/convolution interface GS1/GS2, and Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.0/5/7). Construct the two R_G actions on equivariant cohomology, prove the tensor-over-R_G comparison and equality of the actions using minimal generators, and obtain monoidal H* by augmentation. Construct the opposite category and finite-level IC equivalence without assuming its projection perfectly smooth. Construct pinned opposition, open-normalized IC maps and the chosen square-root phase. Import the restricted Lusztig–Yun identity from SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters, proved using GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1 equal-characteristic Satake; import indexing from RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. Prove the mixed IC dimension/trace realization, involution stalk signs, costalk-duality shifts and orbit-filtration argument giving Θ=(-1)^j on IH^(2j). Correct the unshifted IC and additive Koszul conventions, prove that c induces the ordinary flip under H*, and reflect symmetry/hexagon by faithfulness. Export this independent symmetry to the existing GS4 rational equivalence. GS3:fusion, GS4 reconstruction and the mixed equivalence are not prerequisites of this proof. The coarse roadmap cycle must be resolved by these explicit early/late contracts. Test the unit, two odd components, a torus, a rank-one quasi-minuscule resolution, an involution with maximal trace, and a nontrivial boundary stalk. Keep Q̄_ℓ, ℓ≠p, component parity, half-Tate choices and square-root independence explicit. No integral, ramified extension or multi-leg coherence theorem is inferred. Corrections the design must carry: in (2.4.4) the sign is (−1)^{ε₁ε₂} (E15) and in Lemma 2.28 c_vect is the Koszul-signed flip (E57); the proof of Lemma 2.32 must use the equivariant computation in every degree, since H*(Gr_μ) is not generated by H² (E58); and the twisted trace formula for P^{σ,⋄} (p. 454) is asserted, not proved, and needs a proof (E61).

sourceIssues.printed: (v2) 'We have H'xY' -> Y' x_{Y'/H'} Y' -> Y'xY', where the second map is a closed embedding (since Y'/H' is separated), and the first map is finite. Passing to the perfection, we see that H x Y = Y x_{(Y/H')^{p^-inf}} Y [sic]. I.e. Y -> (Y'/H')^{p^-inf} is an H-torsor. Therefore we obtain a map (Y'/H')^{p^-inf} -> [Y/H] which is clearly an isomorphism.'
sourceIssues.correction: (v2 only.) Y -> (Y'/H')^{p^-∞} must be shown to be flat before it can be called an H-torsor. The published version does this: Theorem A.30 uses Corollary A.16 to show V ≅ U x_X U, and Lemma A.31 then gives flatness of A^{p^-∞} over C^{p^-∞}, since A^{p^-∞} ⊗_{C^{p^-∞}} A^{p^-∞} = B^{p^-∞} is flat over A^{p^-∞}.
sourceIssues.reason: Checked on the v2 page images (PDF pp. 47-48). The torsor property rests only on the displayed isomorphism, which gives no flatness, and a coarse quotient map by a finite flat groupoid is not flat in general. The conclusion is true (v3 and the published version prove it), so the step is unjustified rather than false: a gap, not an error. Numbering: v2 Prop. The published paper does not have this gap.

review.reason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. On the v2 page images (PDF pp. 47-48) the quoted passage is verbatim, including the malformed 'H x Y ≃ Y_{(Y/H')^{p^-∞}} Y'. The torsor claim 'I.e. Y -> (Y'/H')^{p^-∞} is an H-torsor' rests only on the isomorphism H x Y ≃ Y x_M Y (M the perfected coarse space). By the paper's own definition (A.1.3, p. 468) a torsor also needs an fpqc, in particular flat, projection, and nothing in the v2 argument gives flatness. The displayed isomorphism cannot give it on its own: with H trivial it only says Y -> M is a monomorphism, e.g. the perfection of Spec k ⊔ (A^1 minus 0) -> A^1, which is surjective but not flat. Coarse quotients by finite flat groupoids are not flat in general (A^2 -> A^2/{±1}). The conclusion is nevertheless true. The published proof (Theorem A.29 reduced to Theorem A.30, flatness from Lemma A.31, pp. 476-477, identical in v3 PDF pp. 53-54) proves it. The published argument is complete once one notes that A^{p^-∞} ⊗_{C^{p^-∞}} A^{p^-∞} = B^{p^-∞} is flat over A^{p^-∞}, since B is finite locally free over A, and that ∩ J_k^{p^-∞} = 0 because some power of each element lands in (∏ J_k)R, which lies in the nilradical. So the v2 step is unjustified, not false: a gap in the v2 proof, not an error. The published paper does not have it. I checked the arXiv record myself: v3 is dated 20 Jul 2016 and its comment reads 'Fix a gap in the proof of Theorem A.29. A few more details added'. The numbering correspondence (v2 Prop. A.28 = v3/published Theorem A.29, v2 Lemma A.27 = published Lemma A.28) matches the images.

review.reason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. The page images read 's_{1+θ} is the affine reflection corresponding to 1 + θ' (statement of Lemma 2.12(ii), p. 437) and 'the only affine root appearing in Q_{1/2} but not in Q_{1/4} is −θ − 1' (proof, p. 438). I recomputed from the definition on p. 437: U_α(ϖ^kO) ⊂ Q_r iff k ≥ ⌈r⟨θ,α⟩⌉, and ⟨θ,α⟩ ∈ {0,±1,±2}, with ±2 only for α = ±θ^∨. Q_{1/2} and Q_{1/4} differ only at α = −θ^∨ (k ≥ −1 against k ≥ 0), i.e. at the affine root −θ^∨ − 1. Q_{1/2} and Q_{3/4} differ only at θ^∨ (k ≥ 1 against k ≥ 2), i.e. at θ^∨ + 1. So the reductive quotient of Q_{1/2} has an A_1 factor with roots ±(θ^∨+1), and Q_{1/4} and Q_{3/4} map to opposite Borels of it. The reflection s_{θ^∨+1} = s_{−θ^∨−1} (so the sign is irrelevant) fixes −θ/2 and sends −θ/4 to −3θ/4. It conjugates Q_{1/4} to Q_{3/4} and sends ϖ^θ to the base point. Q_{1/4}sQ_{3/4}/Q_{3/4} is the Q_{1/4}-fixed point of Q_{1/2}/Q_{3/4} ≅ P^1, and Q_0 ×^{Q_{1/4}} (that point) = Q_0/Q_{1/4} = Ḡ/P̄_θ maps to Gr_0, as claimed. Only one reading makes sense and it is confirmed by arXiv v2 (p. 21, item (2): 'the hyperplane H given by the affine root 1 + θ^∨'), so the old 'affects: the proof' and the open 'wall sign' question are not warranted. The same text is in v2 and v3. The first occurrence is in the statement of 2.12(ii) on p. 437, the second in the proof on p. 438.

review.reason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: The revision is right. The quotation matches the image of p. 448. By (1.4.5) (p. 429), p is the map to Z/2 written multiplicatively, μ → (-1)^{(2ρ,μ)}, and Lemma 1.25 and p. 448 say its values are 1 or -1. So p(A1)p(A2) is +1 or -1 and (-1)^{p(A1)p(A2)} = -1 for every pair of pure-parity objects. Read literally, c = -c' always, and for A1 = A2 = IC_0 (H^* = Q̄_ℓ in degree 0) Proposition 2.21 would then fail, because H^*(c) = -id is not the flip. The intended formula is the Koszul change (-1)^{ε(A1)ε(A2)}, with ε = (1-p)/2 the additive parity. That is what an additive reading of p in F_2 would give, and it is what the text announces ('by a Koszul sign change') and cites ([BD, 5.3.21], [MV07] after Remark 6.2). So the meaning is recoverable and misprint is the right kind. 'Error' was not coherent with 'affects nothing'. The formula is the same in v2 ((2.4.3)) and v3 ((2.4.4)). The sign bookkeeping works only together with E57: the Koszul change gives Proposition 2.21 exactly because H^*(c') is the Koszul-signed flip.

review.reason: The sentence is an accurate, compressed description of LY13 (published version). The proof of Lemma 4.3 (arXiv 3.3) contains a single sign computation: τ_K^* acts by −1 on H^2 of the orbit's partial flag variety, which is the degree-2 case of the analogue of Zhu's Lemma 2.32 (Zhu, p. 451: 'essentially the same as [LY13, Lemma 3.3]'). With geometric Satake this gives g = (−1)^ρ, hence Lemma 4.3(3) (the analogue of Lemma 2.30), then §4.4/§7.4 (the analogue of Lemma 2.34) and Theorem 1.3/7.3. Zhu states the intermediate step through Lemma 2.30 and geometric Satake explicitly on p. 450 and p. 452, and Remark 2.33 explains why the Chern-class computation alone does not suffice without Satake, so there is no inconsistency. In any case a provenance remark cannot affect Zhu's proof, which uses Theorem 2.35 as a black box. The genuine defect nearby is the LY13 numbering, recorded as a separate new issue. Independent check: I agree with the first reading that this is not a mistake. The sentence on p. 453 matches the image. In LY13 (published version, checked; arXiv 1203.0521v1 is the only arXiv version), Lemma 4.3 (v1: 3.3) takes one geometric input, besides the Satake equivalence. That input is that τ_K^* acts trivially on H^0 and by -1 on H^2 of the partial flag variety K/(P_λ ∩ K) onto which the open orbit retracts. This is the degree <= 2 case of the equal-characteristic analogue of Zhu's Lemma 2.32, and Zhu (p. 451) says his proof of 2.32 is 'essentially the same as [LY13, Lemma 3.3]'. Using IH^i = H^i(open orbit) for i <= 2, and Tannakian arguments with geometric Satake, LY obtain g = (-1)^ρ and hence Lemma 4.3(3), the analogue of Lemma 2.30. Section 4.4 then gives the stalk sign (analogue of Lemma 2.34), and (3.5) gives Theorem 1.3. Section 7.4 reruns this chain for Theorem 7.3, which is Zhu's Theorem 2.35. So 'deduced ... from the equal characteristic analogue of Lemma 2.32' is a compressed but true description. It does not claim that the Chern-class computation suffices on its own. Zhu says explicitly on p. 450 that LY used the equal-characteristic geometric Satake, and Remark 2.33 explains why 2.32 alone does not give 2.30. The ledger's contrary claim, that the argument uses the IH sign theorem (analogue of 2.30), is also true, because that is an intermediate step of the same chain. It does not make Zhu's sentence false. In any case a provenance remark cannot affect Zhu's proof, which uses Theorem 2.35 as a black box, so the ledger's 'affects: the proof' is unfounded. The real defect nearby is the LY13 numbering (E59).
